  appended takes; source revision changes are visible. Manifest schema 5 lists original and prepared workshop JSON
  sidecars clipped/rebased by the common IN/OUT recipe, retaining original coordinates and provenance. These files
  do not publish media or turn transcripts into participant subtitles.
- `/admin/shortener` manages public short links, QR/UTM output, destinations,
  notes, search/filter/sort state, and private click history. Links are served
  by `/[shortcode]`; `/shortener` redirects to the admin page.
- `/admin/login` authenticates the single `admin` account with `ADMIN_PASSWORD`
  and a signed session cookie. All `/admin/*` pages and APIs require
  `requireAdminSignedIn`. `/admin` is the post-login dashboard.
- Other public/legal routes include `/contact`, `/data-deletion`, `/privacy`,
  `/terms`, `/dekujeme`, `/branding`, and the routes under `/k`, `/old`, and
  `/test`.

#### Shared community and workshop behavior

- Workshop occurrences choose video, presentation, or their connected repository as the primary stage source. Old
  data defaults to video; the choice never changes which sources are stored. The countdown and wrap-up still follow
  `workshopPhase.ts`, and other readable sources remain supplementary special materials with recording access chosen
  by the server. Permanent room kinds which have no stage remain without one.

- Community and workshop participant rooms, including waiting rooms and community project views, share light,
  dark, and device appearance through `WorkshopRoomThemeProvider` and `workshopRoomTheme.css`. The browser remembers
  the choice across rooms and tabs; changing it preserves form and room state. Room palette tokens also reach
  portalled membership/project dialogs and cookie controls. Public landing pages and administration keep their own
  appearance.

- The global cookie banner shares its page palette with its settings dialog, uses
  a shallow bottom strip on desktop and an inset panel on phones, and reserves its
  measured height so the end of each page stays reachable. Fixed bottom controls
  such as the podcast player and admin table scrollbar opt into clearance through
  `data-fixed-bottom-control`; the banner, booking notice, and coder badge measure
  their neighbors through `hooks/useFixedControlClearance.ts`.

- Rooms lead to each other in both directions, through one identity hand-off. The
  community lists the terms and opens the room of each; an invited workshop room
  places its community link beside its materials as a special material for every
  participant, regardless of paid membership. Where a special material sits is
  decided once, in `lib/workshops/workshopSpecialMaterials.ts`: a card says where
  among the ordinary materials it belongs, and the invitation opens the material
  list of a participant who does not pay while it closes the list of a paying
  member. A membership which is not loaded yet leaves it where a participant who
  does not pay reads it. Both carry the connected member's
  name and email on, and an incomplete identity carries nothing rather than half
  of it. Which rooms invite is answered by
  `lib/workshops/workshopKindCapabilities.ts`; the community and project
  discussions do not. The invitation names the community's sections by the names
  the community itself uses.
- Community polls attached to workshops are shared. A normalized email gives a
  member one vote across the community and all attached workshops. An
  administrator can enable an Other answer: a member-written response becomes
  one shared, anonymous option and receives that member's vote atomically, so
  every room can vote for it; later poll edits keep member-written answers.
  Such an answer goes through the very moderation a chat message does, by the
  one shared submission policy in `lib/workshops/workshopSubmissionStatus.ts`:
  it is pending until the shared AI review or a moderator approves it, while a trusted member and a
  moderator have theirs approved as they write it. The vote of its writer is
  counted at once either way, but until the answer is approved only its writer
  and the moderators of the room owning the poll receive it or its vote, and a
  rejected answer is gone for everybody. Who may read one answer is decided
  once, in `lib/workshops/workshopPollOptionVisibility.ts`.
  Workshops may display and accept votes, but the community owns administration.
  Where a room puts its polls is decided once, in
  `lib/workshops/workshopPollPlacement.ts`: the community, which decides in its
  own polls, opens with them, while a workshop, which is only their subject,
  keeps them below the materials it was held for.
- The participant room owns the membership badge and popup. Community and live
  workshop rooms use the same membership for the connecting email, and checkout
  returns to the room where it started. Membership is offered only by room kinds
  listed in `lib/workshops/workshopKindCapabilities.ts`; project discussions do
  not offer it.
- Members can open Stripe Customer Portal from the popup. In-app cancellation
  stops only the next renewal, preserves access through the paid period, appears
  in the badge, and can be reversed before that period ends.
- A full-price-for-the-whole-term discount is a voucher: atomically consume it,
  create membership immediately, ask for no card, and create no Stripe renewal.
  A limited-month discount still opens checkout because the regular price returns.
  Stripe webhooks update completed, cancelled, failed, and late payments. With no
  Stripe key, hide membership; with test keys, identify the test payment gate.
- Community projects use a URL-first metadata wizard. Ordinary submissions await
  AI or manual moderation; trusted members and moderators are approved immediately. Pending
  projects remain visible to their author and moderators.
- A live workshop room has a countdown before it starts and, while it runs, the
  event's selected primary stage content: video, presentation, or the connected
  repository. Existing and unset choices mean video. Other configured sources
  stay in the shared special-material list, with recordings still selected by
  the server's member access rule. After the recorded end, the stage returns to
  the wrap-up. Permanent rooms such as the community do not gain a stage. The
  room also has reactions, watching count, moderated chat, timed materials, and
  attached poll aggregates. An open-ended term runs until its recorded end; its
  stage does not end automatically. Admins
  can select, replace, clear, or create the displayed comment through the same
  private realtime channel used by reactions.
- Workshop and community chat can use reusable Book agents, administered in their shared Agents tab with
  `BookEditor` from `@promptbook/components`. `LiteAgent` from `@promptbook/node` uses `OPENAI_API_KEY`; definitions
  are shared while replies, listening and cooldowns are enabled per room. Only newly approved comments enqueue
  replies, including artificial and other agent messages, with at most two agent turns. A durable database queue
  owns leases, deduplication and rechecks of moderation, agent settings and room state before publication.
  Public messages use the existing chat rendering; admin projections and exports distinguish `user`, `artificial`
  and `agent` origins with agent/run provenance. Agents have no participant sessions or membership access.
  Live questions require an administrator's active stream-tab or microphone capture in the Agents tab; audio is
  transcribed in short standalone segments and never saved. Private transcripts feed the agents only during an
  ongoing workshop and only from its current, unexpired capture session. Stopping capture or ending the workshop
  prevents its pending live questions from publishing; publication locks that session against a concurrent stop.
  Project rooms and externally organized events offer no agents. Persistent servers run the queue in the background;
  serverless hosts can use the authenticated scheduler route documented in `README.md`.
- A term can be about a project. The connection is one value — GitHub repository,
  the default branch, and one or more branch patterns such as `main`, `client-*`,
  `feature/*`, or `*` for all branches, plus any number of public deployment
  addresses, written one per line — so it is set, changed, and unset at once and
  neither branch selection nor deployment
  outlives its repository. Room kinds which offer it are named in
  `lib/workshops/workshopKindCapabilities.ts`. The room shows the repository as a
  special material beside its ordinary materials for every participant, with its
  links, every deployment and newest commits, marking those which arrive while a
  participant watches;
  a newly found commit is broadcast to active rooms and appears on the stage for
  ten seconds. A selection resolving to multiple branches is shown as a commit
  graph. Commits come from the public commit feed or keyless API, pooled once per
  server and cached through the revalidation window; an unreadable feed still
  leaves the room naming its project. A project deployed once is opened as the live
  application of the workshop; several deployments are each named by their own
  address, and the first of them is the one a term card and the participant project panel are previewed from.
  Both reuse the deployment's image, title and description through the shared project preview; missing metadata or
  a broken image keeps the deployment address visible, with repository-only previews reserved for undeployed projects.
  The participant preview opens that deployment and loads independently of room state and commits, through an
  authenticated endpoint using the stored project. Changing rooms, repositories or the primary deployment discards
  stale previews. Community term cards keep their workshop destination.
  With a repository and no deployment URL, administration offers direct Vercel deployment using private `VERCEL_TOKEN`
  and optional `VERCEL_TEAM_ID`. One Vercel project per repository stays connected to its original GitHub source and
  deploys its production branch (initially the default branch), independently of the workshop's history selection.
  Administration polls the build and fills in its assigned production alias only when ready; the ordinary settings
  save publishes that URL. Manual URLs, a changed repository, and switching rooms discard stale pending results.
  Deployment failures show the reported reason and code, targeted recovery steps, and an optional bounded build-log
  excerpt with credentials redacted. Canceled, blocked, and alias-assignment failures have distinct guidance; missing
  diagnostics keep fallback checks and the Vercel link available. Only authenticated administration receives them.
  This adds no workshop data fields; setup and retry behavior are documented in `README.md`.
  The connection can also carry independent starting and ending commit IDs. Administration previews each commit's
  message, author and Prague date, and can fill each bound separately from the workshop time (first commit at or after
  the start, last at or before the end). Bounds are inclusive by commit time across the selected branches. The room
  initially shows and highlights that range; expanding and paging its graph reveals history outside it while retaining
  the highlight. An omitted bound leaves that side open; two omitted bounds leave the history unfiltered. Every lookup,
  autofill and history page uses the same branch selection, and commits belonging only to other branches stay hidden.
- A workshop can carry one public presentation URL for a PDF, PowerPoint file, or
  GitHub Markdown page. The room renders it beside ordinary materials through the
  shared material card, primary action, preview card and flip-to-show QR code, for every participant without making
  it timed or membership-gated content.
- Paid-only materials are decided on the server in one pass. Members receive
  unlocked material; others receive only the published titles as an offer. An
  untitled item is not named, items are not named before their unlock time, and a
  room without membership hides paid-only items without naming them.
- After a workshop ends, its recording is server-gated to members. Others receive
  the published teaser, or a generic offer when no teaser exists; a term without
  a recording offers nothing. An administrator writes the recording's start
  offset as hours, minutes and seconds, while it stays stored, exported and read
  in seconds; it applies only to that paid replay and never to the countdown or
  live stream.
  A workshop can instead select a hosted synchronized recording while preserving its inactive YouTube settings.
  Direct admin import and studio publication use the same private multipart object storage and schema 5 validation;
  verified revisions publish atomically, and old revisions remain briefly for connected viewers. Room JSON and every
  hosted manifest/range request apply the same live/free and paid replay rule. Prepared hosted media uses export zero,
  with recorded pause gaps mapped to the chosen live wall clock; the YouTube offset is never applied again. Imported
  subtitle sidecars stay out of the participant player. Cleanup claims inactive revisions before removing objects.
  The hosted participant player uses one prepared-export clock across Auto, Editor, Aplikace and Kamera, with a camera
  overlay in Auto, reviewed activity speed boundaries, event markers and anchored commit selection in the existing
  repository graph. Auto speed advances automatic-coding intervals through decoded steps at up to 10× and waits when
  decoding is slower. Free live playback serves only the completed, at-most-two-second segment at the server-delayed playhead through a
  time-authorized route; direct full-file bytes and other segments are denied. Members may seek the full published
  recording. Complete publication is required before this scheduled live delivery; it is not an ingest stream.
- Pending chat messages, member-written poll answers, and community projects use
  `lib/workshops/workshopAutoApproval.ts` for optional AI approval after saving.
  `WORKSHOP_AUTO_APPROVAL_API_KEY` enables it; the model and HTTPS base URL are
  configurable. Only clearly suitable content is approved; uncertainty, missing
  configuration, invalid output, and an eight-second timeout leave it pending.
  The database approves only unchanged pending content from a currently unbanned
  author and privately records the item, model, and time. AI never rejects, edits,
  grants trust, or replaces a human decision. It reviews text and URL metadata,
  without fetching linked pages or preview images. Moderator-created materials
  require no review, and old pending submissions are not bulk-processed.
- Trusted participants remain invisible and their messages are auto-approved.
  The participant lists in workshop and community administration show three exclusive, complete room counts:
  moderators, trusted non-moderators, and untrusted non-moderators. Their explicit bulk-trust action confirms a
  server-reviewed eligible set and updates that room atomically; a changed set requires a fresh confirmation.
  The separate automatic-trust setting defaults off for every new or duplicated room and is applied only when a new
  participant identity is inserted. Reconnects and later setting changes never rewrite an existing trust decision.
  Granting trust or moderator status also approves every pending submission by that room-local participant — chat,
  member-written poll answers, and community projects — in the same database transaction. Rejected items stay
  rejected; a ban blocks this approval until it is lifted. The private pending-submission view supplies both this
  approval and the complete per-person counts in room moderation and administrative participant lists. Community
  project cards refresh with the room without resetting the submission form.
  Moderators see pending messages, can approve/reject/correct/pin them, and can
  trust or silence authors. An administrator in `/admin/workshops` and a moderator
  in a workshop room can also turn any comment into an ordinary, immediately
  available material. That preserves the comment in chat, carries its complete
  Markdown body into the material, and names its author in the material title;
  both entry points use the shared material creation path, including its short
  links and room refresh. Workshop and community moderators are appointed in
  `/admin/workshops`; project authors moderate their own discussions.
- The room records whether each open browser is actively or passively attended
  from pointer, typing, scroll, and touch activity. Admin analytics distinguish
  active computer users from merely open tabs with dashed audience lines.
- The community's compact gallery shows its five highest-upvoted approved projects
  and links to the full gallery. Community landing content is read from the live
  room: expose only anonymous totals, approved messages, and shared projects;
  show member first names only. If the room cannot be read, show less content,
  not an error. Landing-page reactions are estimates based on recent room data.

#### Administration and data rules

- Workshop and community settings render their shared `WorkshopSettingsForm` directly in the Settings tab,
  with autosave and navigation protection. Other admin creation and editing use the shared `AdminEditorDialog`
  (and `AdminEditorButton` for a local trigger).
  Lists show summaries and edit actions; contact notes and contacted status are edited in the contact dialog.
  The dialog contains request errors, traps and restores focus, and scrolls within the viewport. Closing with its
  button or Escape flushes pending saves and keeps invalid or failed drafts open; backdrop clicks preserve the editor.
  Search, filters, and immediate moderation actions stay in their lists. New records still require explicit creation.

- Existing records in `/admin` autosave through `useAdminAutosave` and the shared `AdminSaveQueue`.
  Raw drafts remain dirty through validation failures and failed requests; writes are debounced and serialized,
  and polling must not replace an editor's draft. Editors stay open after autosave. Pending writes protect
  close/reload with the browser's native warning; admin links, section/record switches, and sign-out flush saves
  before leaving. Explicit API mutations share `requestAdminJson`/`protectAdminMutation` for in-flight protection.
  Creation and destructive actions remain explicit. Keep record editors keyed by their stable database identity.
  Immediate material unlocking shares its draft save. Poll updates return generated prepared-choice IDs; the editor
  carries them into subsequent saves while preserving newer text, so autosaving never recreates a saved choice.

- Event kinds are defined once in `lib/events/eventTypes.ts`; adding one should
  not require database migration or page-specific duplication. Terms ask for kind,
  online/place format, price, and capacity. Each kind also names where its landing
  page records registrations, which is the `placeName` of the contacts it gathers.
  A kind which names no landing page is held by somebody else: its terms carry the
  address they are held at, are refused without one, and this application runs no
  room, gathers no registration, and returns no payer to them.
- Which term a registration belongs to is decided once, in
  `lib/workshops/workshopRegistrations.ts`. A term is recognised by its slug, by
  its Prague day, and by the moment it begins at, so registrations written before
  terms had slugs keep counting. Registration forms write the term through the
  same line prefixes that rule reads back. Contacts are still gathered, recorded
  and shown only by `/admin/contacts`; counting reads nothing but their notes.
  The registration actions in workshop administration carry that same term filter
  into the contacts list and its exports.
- Workshop polls are read-only in workshop administration, except for the
  answers members wrote into them: an administrator approves, rejects, rewords,
  or deletes one together with the votes cast for it, and reads it named by the
  author who wrote it, while a moderator of the room owning the poll only
  decides about it from the room itself. Creating a new event
  publishes it by default; duplicating an event keeps it published unless the
  source is unpublished. Duplicating a workshop preserves its connections to
  the already existing attached polls; it creates no polls, options, votes, or room history. Stage settings contain
  the live stream, paid-recording start offset, and recording teaser; presentation settings the public presentation
  address, and project settings the repository the term is about, written as an
  address or as `owner/name`, together with its branch patterns. Deleting a workshop is a soft deletion: its room
  data and attached
  community polls stay stored, but the term leaves normal public and administrative
  lists and no longer holds its slug for a replacement. An end may be empty;
  admins can record, adjust, clear, and reopen it. Overview analytics are zoomable and share their
  room, section, lines, reaction, zoom, and keyword metrics through query params.
- Community administration is the workshop dashboard restricted to the
  `community` room kind: no room picker, schedule, stage, reactions, or address.
  Its membership view filters Stripe lifecycle, prices, discounts, identifiers,
  dates, test/live mode, and links to the exact Stripe checkout/subscription.
  Community analytics cover all measured time and member details show seen times.
- Shortener search, provenance filters, sorting, and selected click history live
  in GET parameters. Editing changes only shortcode, destinations, note, and
  landing page; deletion also deletes recorded clicks.

#### Database and verification

- Put database changes in `migrations/*.sql`. Startup and
  `npm run migrate-database` run `_initialize.sql`, then migrations in filename
  order, recording immutable filenames and checksums in `public."Migration"`.
  Changed or missing migrations fail, as do queries requiring an unapplied one.
- `npm run test-types` must build before `tsc` to refresh `.next/types`.
- `npm run test-e2e` uses the Next.js development server; first-request compile
  headroom belongs in `playwright.config.ts`, not individual tests. E2E tests are
  independent and retry once in a fresh browser context for transient failures;
  failed-attempt traces remain available. Each attempt archives one recording in
  `tests/e2e/videos/`, retaining only recent runs.
- Recording-studio E2E sources use canvas video and synthesized audio with a silent Web Audio output, independent
  of physical audio-device clocks. Keep recording, storage, codecs, trimming, and ZIP exports real in these tests.
  Recorded A/V markers are checked from decoded sample timestamps rather than speaker-output latency. The preparation
  fixture additionally carries readable/binary timecodes and claps at 25/30 fps with distinct startup offsets.
  Simulated ten-hour mappings and decoder delays do not establish a ten-hour capture soak or physical macOS behavior.

Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: \"chart\", \"graph\", \"plot\", \"data viz\", \"visualization\", \"dashboard\", \"analytics\", \"visualize data\", \"categorical colors\", \"sequential / diverging palette\", \"stat tile\", \"sparkline\", \"heatmap\", \"legend\", \"axis\", \"tooltip\", \"chart colors\", \"color by series\".","argumentHint":"","builtin":true},{"name":"update-config","description":"Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. from '@/lib/events/eventPrice';\nimport {\n    formatCzechWorkshopDay,\n    formatCzechWorkshopDayAndMonth,\n    formatCzechWorkshopTimeRange,\n} from '@/lib/workshops/workshopDate';\n\nconst EVENT_DETAIL_SEPARATOR = ' · ';\nconst EVENT_DAY_SEPARATOR = ' / ';\nconst EVENT_LOCATION_SEPARATOR = ' i ';\n\n/**\n * The same values in the order they were first written, so a summary never repeats in any particular order, so withdrawing a term never leaves a page describing a term which is not offered.\n */\nexport function findEventOccurrenceByLocationKind(\n    occurrences: readonly * The days a set of terms is held on, for example `4. 9. / 9. 9. / 18. 9.`\n */\nexport function formatEventOccurrenceDaySummary(occurrences: readonly EventOccurrence[]): string {\n    return selectDistinctValues(\n        occurrences.map((occurrence) => formatCzechWorkshopDayAndMonth(occurrence.startsAt)),\n    ).join(EVENT_DAY_SEPARATOR);\n}\n\n/**\n * Where a set of terms is held, for {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_016vFdYuRcT4odruEixWrdUz","type":"tool_result","content":"1\timport { COMMUNITY_CALENDAR_PATH } from '@/businesses/community/config';\n2\timport type { WorkshopConnectionDetails } from '@/businesses/online-workshop/participant/WorkshopConnectionForm';\n3\timport { createAbsoluteUrl } from '@/lib/metadata/site-config';\n4\timport type { WorkshopDetails } from '@/lib/workshops/workshopTypes';\n5\t\n6\t/**\n7\t * What the door of the community says, wherever it is offered\n8\t *\n9\t * Note: The connection form of the community and the invitation which leads to it from another room are the same door,\n10\t *       so they say the same words rather than two variations of them.\n11\t */\n12\tconst CZECH_COMMUNITY_ENTRY_LABEL = 'Vstoupit do komunity';\n13\t\n14\t/**\n15\t * Keeps Czech community copy beside the Czech route. A future English route can provide its own factory without\n16\t * duplicating the room mechanics or tying a translation to a database row.\n17\t */\n18\texport function createCzechCommunityConnectionDetails(community: WorkshopDetails): WorkshopConnectionDetails {\n19\t    return {\n20\t        title: community.title,\n21\t        description: community.description,\n22\t        dateLabel: 'Kdykoli online',\n23\t        durationLabel: 'Stálý přístup',\n24\t        roomLabel: 'Komunita Promptbooku',\n25\t        connectionHeading: 'Připojit se do komunity',\n26\t        connectionDescription: 'Jméno se zobrazí u vašich komentářů. E-mail ostatní členové komunity neuvidí.',\n27\t        submitLabel: CZECH_COMMUNITY_ENTRY_LABEL,\n28\t        language: 'cs',\n29\t    };\n30\t}\n31\t\n32\t/**\n33\t * How the permanent community names its own sections\n34\t *\n35\t * Note: Every section of the community is named exactly once here, so an invitation into the community from elsewhere\n36\t *       promises what is waiting there under the very name it carries once a member arrives.\n37\t */\n38\texport const CZECH_COMMUNITY_ROOM_COPY = {\n39\t    roomSubtitle: 'Komunita Promptbooku',\n40\t    materialsTitle: 'Materiály komunity',\n41\t    projectsTitle: 'Projekty komunity',\n42\t    unavailableConnectionMessage: 'Připojení ke komunitě se nepodařilo ověřit.',\n43\t} as const;\n44\t\n45\texport const CZECH_COMMUNITY_WORKSHOP_NAVIGATION_COPY = {\n46\t    title: 'Termíny akcí Promptbooku',\n47\t    description:\n48\t        'Vyberte si termín v kalendáři nebo v kartách. Odkaz vás vezme přímo do místnosti workshopu se stejnými údaji, u placených akcí na jejich stránku a u externích akcí na web pořadatele.',\n49\t    emptyMessage: 'Zatím není publikovaný žádný termín. A future English route can provide its own factory without\n * duplicating the room mechanics or tying a translation to a database row.\n */\nexport function createCzechCommunityConnectionDetails(community: WorkshopDetails): WorkshopConnectionDetails {\n    return {\n        title: community.title,\n        description: community.description,\n        dateLabel: 'Kdykoli online',\n        durationLabel: 'Stálý přístup',\n        roomLabel: 'Komunita Promptbooku',\n        connectionHeading: 'Připojit se do komunity',\n        connectionDescription: 'Jméno se zobrazí u vašich komentářů. Další sem přidáme hned po zveřejnění.',\n    locale: 'cs-CZ',\n    timeZone: 'Europe/Prague',\n    calendarFeedUrl: createAbsoluteUrl(COMMUNITY_CALENDAR_PATH),\n} as const;\n\n/**\n * How a room which is no community itself invites its participants into the permanent one\n *\n * Note: What waits there is named by the sections of the community room rather than by words written here, so the\n *       invitation can never promise something the community itself calls differently.\n */\nexport const CZECH_COMMUNITY_INVITATION_COPY = {\n    eyebrow: CZECH_COMMUNITY_ROOM_COPY.roomSubtitle,\n    title: 'Pokračujte s námi v komunitě',\n    description:\n        'Workshop jednou skončí, komunita běží pořád. Chat zůstává otevřený, ostatní členové tam sdílejí, na čem pracují, a všechny další termíny najdete na jednom místě.',\n    sectionTitles: [\n        CZECH_COMMUNITY_ROOM_COPY.projectsTitle,\n        CZECH_COMMUNITY_ROOM_COPY.materialsTitle,\n        CZECH_COMMUNITY_WORKSHOP_NAVIGATION_COPY.title,\n    ],\n    linkLabel: CZECH_COMMUNITY_ENTRY_LABEL,\n} as const;\n","numLines":73,"startLine":1,"totalLines":73}}}

built from\n     */\n    readonly occurrence: WorkshopCalendarOccurrence;\n\n    /**\n     * Full name of the person who leads the workshop\n     */\n    readonly hostFullname: string;\n\n    /**\n rest of their day\n *\n * @returns title such as `Karel <> Pavol - Produkční kód s AI agenty`, shortened whenever one of the names is missing\n */\nexport function createWorkshopCalendarEventTitle(\n    workshopTitle: string,\n    hostFullname: string,\n    participantFullname: string,\n): string {\n    const meetingTitle = [getFirstName(participantFullname), getFirstName(hostFullname)]\n        .filter((firstName) => firstName !== '')\n        .join(WORKSHOP_MEETING_SEPARATOR);\n\n    return meetingTitle === '' ? workshopTitle : `${meetingTitle} - ${workshopTitle}`;\n}\n\n/**\n * Moment a {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_012sCPexyETGpEeysTedDA6t","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t'use client';\n2\t\n3\timport { createOnlineWorkshopTermNoteText } from '@/businesses/online-workshop/onlineWorkshopTerms';\n4\timport { EventTermOptionList } from '@/components/events/EventTermOptionList';\n5\timport type { EventOccurrence } from '@/lib/events/eventOccurrence';\n6\timport { groupWorkshopsByPhase, isWorkshopPhaseUpcoming, WORKSHOP_PHASE_VALUES } from '@/lib/workshops/workshopPhase';\n7\timport { ChevronDown, Clock, History, Sparkles } from 'lucide-react';\n8\timport { useId, useMemo, useState } from 'react';\n9\t\n10\t/**\n11\t * What the waiting room says while a participant is choosing which workshop to enter\n12\t */\n13\tconst ONLINE_WORKSHOP_ROOM_TERM_PICKER_COPY = {\n14\t    legend: 'Vyberte si workshop',\n15\t    description: 'Do místnosti kteréhokoli workshopu se dostanete stejným jménem a e-mailem.',\n16\t    noCurrentTermsMessage: 'Právě teď žádný workshop neběží a další termín zatím není vypsaný.',\n17\t    freshlyPastTermsLabel: 'Právě proběhlo',\n18\t    pastTermsLabel: 'Proběhlé workshopy',\n19\t\n20\t    /**\n21\t     * Note: A workshop which has only just been held promises exactly what any finished one does, and says only that\n22\t     *       it was now — what a participant came back for is waiting behind the very same open door.\n23\t     */\n24\t    freshlyPastTermNoteText: 'Právě skončil, místnost zůstává otevřená',\n25\t\n26\t    /**\n27\t     * Note: A room which is over is worth entering for what stayed in it, and that is all this promises. tokens.map((token): Content => {\n        const markdownToken = token as MarkedToken;\n        switch (markdownToken.type) {\n            case 'strong':\n            case 'em':\n            case 'del':\n                return {\n                    text: renderInlineTokens(markdownToken.tokens, baseUrl),\n                    bold: markdownToken.type === 'strong' ? true : undefined,\n                    italics: markdownToken.type === 'em' ? true : undefined,\n                    decoration: markdownToken.type === 'del' ? 'lineThrough' : undefined,\n                };\n            case 'link':\n            case 'image': {\n                // Images stay as labelled links: generating a recap never fetches remote resources.\n                const label = readMarkdownTokenText(markdownToken) || markdownToken.href;\n                const link = createPdfLink(label, markdownToken.href, baseUrl);\n                return {\n                    ...link,\n                    text: link.link !== undefined && label !== link.link ? `${label} (${link.link})` : label,\n                };\n            }\n            case 'codespan':\n                return { text: markdownToken.text, background: '#edf2f4' };\n            case 'text':\n                return markdownToken.tokens === undefined\n                    ? readMarkdownTokenText(markdownToken)\n                    : { text: renderInlineTokens(markdownToken.tokens, baseUrl) };\n            default:\n                return readMarkdownTokenText(markdownToken);\n        }\n    });\n}\n\nfunction renderTable(token: Tokens.Table, baseUrl: string): Content {\n    const renderCell = (cell: Tokens.TableCell): Content => ({\n        text: renderInlineTokens(cell.tokens, baseUrl),\n        bold: cell.header,\n        alignment: cell.align ?? 'left',\n    });\n    return {\n        table: {\n            headerRows: 1,\n            widths: token.header.map(() => '*'),\n            body: [token.header.map(renderCell), ...token.rows.map((row) => row.map(renderCell))],\n        },\n        layout: 'lightHorizontalLines',\n        margin: [0, 4, 0, 10],\n    };\n}\n\nfunction renderBlockTokens(tokens: readonly Token[], baseUrl: string): Content[] {\n    return tokens.flatMap((token): Content[] => {\n        const markdownToken = token as MarkedToken;\n        switch (markdownToken.type) {\n            case 'space':\n            case 'def':\n                return [];\n            case 'heading':\n                return [\n                    {\n                        text: renderInlineTokens(markdownToken.tokens, baseUrl),\n                        fontSize: Math.max(11, 17 - markdownToken.depth),\n                        bold: true,\n                        margin: [0, 10, 0, 5],\n                    },\n                ];\n            case 'list': {\n                const items = markdownToken.items.map(\n                    (item): Content => ({\n                        stack: [\n                            ...(item.task ? [{ text: item.checked ? '[x]' : '[ ]' }] : []),\n                            ...renderBlockTokens(item.tokens, baseUrl),\n                        ],\n                    }),\n                );\n                return [\n                    markdownToken.ordered\n                        ? { ol: items, start: Number(markdownToken.start) || 1, margin: [0, 0, 0, 8] }\n                        : { ul: items, margin: [0, 0, 0, 8] },\n                ];\n            }\n            case 'blockquote':\n                return [\n                    { stack: renderBlockTokens(markdownToken.tokens, baseUrl), margin: [12, 4, 0, 8], italics: true },\n                ];\n            case 'code':\n                return [{ text: markdownToken.text, fontSize: 9, background: '#edf2f4', margin: [0, 4, 0, 10] }];\n            case 'table':\n                return [renderTable(markdownToken, baseUrl)];\n            case 'hr':\n                return [{ text: '—', color: '#718096', margin: [0, 4, 0, 4] }];\n            default:\n                return [\n                    {\n                        text:\n                            'tokens' in markdownToken && markdownToken.tokens !== undefined\n                                ? renderInlineTokens(markdownToken.tokens, baseUrl)\n                                : readMarkdownTokenText(markdownToken),\n                        margin: [0, 0, 0, 8],\n                    },\n                ];\n        }\n    });\n}\n\n/** Converts material Markdown into flowing, searchable PDF text with links, lists and tables. */\nexport function createMarkdownPdfContent(markdown: string, baseUrl: string): Content[] {\n    return renderBlockTokens(readMarkdownTokens(markdown), baseUrl);\n}\n","numLines":132,"startLine":1,"totalLines":132}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01MuEuCohPk7zjPA82JvBVvp","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t/**\n2\t * @vitest-environment jsdom\n3\t */\n4\t\n5\timport { WorkshopCommentMarkdown } from '@/components/workshop-comment-markdown';\n6\timport { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';\n7\timport React from 'react';\n8\timport { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';\n9\t\n10\tdescribe('workshop comment Markdown', () => {\n11\t    it('renders only the supported text formatting and leaves rich content inert', () => {\n12\t        const { container } = render(\n13\t            <WorkshopCommentMarkdown content={'**tučně** *kurzíva* __podtržení__ <img src=\"bad\"> ![obrázek](https://bad.example)'} />,\n14\t        );\n15\t\n16\t        expect(screen.getByText('tučně').tagName).toBe('STRONG');\n17\t        expect(screen.getByText('kurzíva').tagName).toBe('EM');\n18\t        expect(screen.getByText('podtržení').tagName).toBe('U');\n19\t        expect(container.querySelector('img')).toBeNull();\n20\t        expect(container.querySelector('a')).toBeNull();\n21\t        expect(container.textContent).toContain('<img src=\"bad\">');\n22\t        expect(container.textContent).toContain('![obrázek](https://bad.example)');\n23\t    });\n24\t\n25\t    it('activates only persisted shortcode URLs when a trusted source explicitly enables links', () => {\n26\t        const content =\n27\t            '[Otevřít návod](https://ptbk.io/moderator-guide) a https://ptbk.io/moderator-video. Původní https://example.com/raw zůstává textem.';\n28\t        const { container, rerender } = render(<WorkshopCommentMarkdown content={content} />);\n29\t\n30\t        expect(container.querySelector('a')).toBeNull();\n31\t\n32\t        rerender(<WorkshopCommentMarkdown content={content} isLinksEnabled />);\n33\t\n34\t        const links = screen.getAllByRole('link');\n35\t        expect(links.map((link) => link.getAttribute('href'))).toEqual([\n36\t            'https://ptbk.io/moderator-guide',\n37\t            'https://ptbk.io/moderator-video',\n38\t        ]);\n39\t        expect(links.every((link) => link.getAttribute('target') === '_blank')).toBe(true);\n40\t        expect(links.every((link) => link.getAttribute('rel') === 'noopener noreferrer')).toBe(true);\n41\t        expect(container.textContent).toContain('https://example.com/raw');\n42\t    });\n43\t\n44\t    it('keeps shortcode-looking text inert inside code, images, and HTML', () => {\n45\t        const { container } = render(\n46\t            <WorkshopCommentMarkdown\n47\t                isLinksEnabled\n48\t                content={'`https://ptbk.io/code` ![obrázek](https://ptbk.io/image) <a href=\"https://ptbk.io/html\">HTML</a>'}\n49\t            />,\n50\t        );\n51\t\n52\t        expect(container.querySelector('a')).toBeNull();\n53\t        expect(container.querySelector('img')).toBeNull();\n54\t    });\n55\t});\n56\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7617c150-9970-4c4e-a550-2e76c168f7b8","uuid":"ebb79204-cdf3-4b9f-9db0-e666d0940c26","timestamp":"2026-10-02T09:12:07.994Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\me\\work\\promptbook-experiments-and-landing-pages\\aldaron\\components\\workshop-comment-markdown.test.tsx","content":"/**\n * @vitest-environment jsdom\n */\n\nimport { WorkshopCommentMarkdown } from '@/components/workshop-comment-markdown';\nimport { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';\nimport React from 'react';\nimport { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';\n\ndescribe('workshop comment Markdown', () => {\n    it('renders only the supported text formatting and leaves rich content inert', () => {\n        const { container } = render(\n            <WorkshopCommentMarkdown content={'**tučně** *kurzíva* __podtržení__ <img src=\"bad\"> ![obrázek](https://bad.example)'} />,\n        );\n\n        expect(screen.getByText('tučně').tagName).toBe('STRONG');\n        expect(screen.getByText('kurzíva').tagName).toBe('EM');\n        expect(screen.getByText('podtržení').tagName).toBe('U');\n        expect(container.querySelector('img')).toBeNull();\n        expect(container.querySelector('a')).toBeNull();\n        expect(container.textContent).toContain('<img src=\"bad\">');\n        expect(container.textContent).toContain('![obrázek](https://bad.example)');\n    });\n\n    it('activates only persisted shortcode URLs when a trusted source explicitly enables links', () => {\n        const content =\n            '[Otevřít návod](https://ptbk.io/moderator-guide) a https://ptbk.io/moderator-video. Původní https://example.com/raw zůstává textem.';\n        const { container, rerender } = render(<WorkshopCommentMarkdown content={content} />);\n\n        expect(container.querySelector('a')).toBeNull();\n\n        rerender(<WorkshopCommentMarkdown content={content} isLinksEnabled />);\n\n        const links = screen.getAllByRole('link');\n        expect(links.map((link) => link.getAttribute('href'))).toEqual([\n            'https://ptbk.io/moderator-guide',\n            'https://ptbk.io/moderator-video',\n        ]);\n        expect(links.every((link) => link.getAttribute('target') === '_blank')).toBe(true);\n        expect(links.every((link) => link.getAttribute('rel') === 'noopener noreferrer')).toBe(true);\n        expect(container.textContent).toContain('https://example.com/raw');\n    });\n\n    it('keeps shortcode-looking text inert inside code, images, and HTML', () => {\n        const { container } = render(\n            <WorkshopCommentMarkdown\n                isLinksEnabled\n                content={'`https://ptbk.io/code` ![obrázek](https://ptbk.io/image) <a href=\"https://ptbk.io/html\">HTML</a>'}\n            />,\n        );\n\n        expect(container.querySelector('a')).toBeNull();\n        expect(container.querySelector('img')).toBeNull();\n    });\n});\n","numLines":56,"startLine":1,"totalLines":56}}}

Produkční kód s AI agenty',\n        );\n        expect(createWorkshopCalendarEventTitle('Produkční kód s AI agenty', '', '')).toBe('Produkční kód s AI agenty');\n    });\n\n    it('points the event to the participant room with the details of the participant prefilled', () => {\n        const event = createWorkshopCalendarEvent({\n            occurrence: ONLINE_WORKSHOP_OCCURRENCE,\n            hostFullname: 'Pavol Hejný',\n            participantIdentity: { email: 'karel@firma.cz', fullname: 'Karel Novák' },\n            participantPath: PARTICIPANT_PATH,\n        });\n\n        const eventUrl = new URL(event.url);\n        expect(eventUrl.pathname).toBe(PARTICIPANT_PATH);\n        expect(eventUrl.searchParams.get('workshop')).toBe(ONLINE_WORKSHOP_OCCURRENCE.slug);\n        expect(eventUrl.searchParams.get('email')).toBe('karel@firma.cz');\n        expect(eventUrl.searchParams.get('fullname')).toBe('Karel Novák');\n        expect(event.title).toBe('Karel <> Pavol - Produkční kód s AI agenty');\n        expect(event.id).toBe(ONLINE_WORKSHOP_OCCURRENCE.slug);\n        expect(event.endsAt).toBe(ONLINE_WORKSHOP_OCCURRENCE.endsAt);\n    });\n\n    it('falls back to the plain participant room when the identity cannot prefill the connection form', () => {\n        const event = createWorkshopCalendarEvent({\n            occurrence: ONLINE_WORKSHOP_OCCURRENCE,\n            hostFullname: 'Pavol Hejný',\n            participantIdentity: { email: '', fullname: 'Karel Novák' },\n            participantPath: PARTICIPANT_PATH,\n        });\n\n        expect(new URL(event.url).searchParams.get('workshop')).toBe(ONLINE_WORKSHOP_OCCURRENCE.slug);\n        expect(event.title).toBe('Karel <> Pavol - Produkční kód s AI agenty');\n    });\n\n    it('gives a workshop without an end its usual length', () => {\n        const event = createWorkshopCalendarEvent({\n            occurrence: { ...ONLINE_WORKSHOP_OCCURRENCE, endsAt: null },\n            hostFullname: 'Pavol Hejný',\n            participantIdentity: { email: 'karel@firma.cz', fullname: 'Karel Novák' },\n            participantPath: PARTICIPANT_PATH,\n        });\n\n        expect(Date.parse(event.endsAt) - Date.parse(event.startsAt)).toBe(60 * 60 * 1000);\n    });\n\n    it('names the downloaded file after the workshop', () => {\n        expect(createWorkshopCalendarFileName('online-workshop-2026-08-20')).toBe('online-workshop-2026-08-20.ics');\n    });\n\n    it('offers the calendar only until the workshop starts', () => {\n        expect(isWorkshopUpcoming('2026-08-20T19:00:00+02:00', '2026-08-20T18:59:59+02:00')).toBe(true);\n        expect(isWorkshopUpcoming('2026-08-20T19:00:00+02:00', '2026-08-20T19:00:00+02:00')).toBe(false);\n        expect(isWorkshopUpcoming('2026-08-20T19:00:00+02:00', '2026-08-20T19:30:00+02:00')).toBe(false);\n    });\n});\n","numLines":85,"startLine":1,"totalLines":85}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01HH9makFxNoSyEsH6VrzDsW","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t/**\n2\t * Product identifier announced in the generated iCalendar file\n3\t */\n4\tconst ICALENDAR_PRODUCT_ID = '-//Promptbook//Landing page//CS';\n5\t\n6\t/**\n7\t * Percent encoded CRLF pair which the iCalendar format requires between its lines\n8\t *\n9\t * Note: The separator is kept in its encoded form on purpose. A plain `\\r\\n` string does not survive the build - the\n10\t *       minifier is free to fold it into a template literal, where the language specification normalizes it down to a\n11\t *       bare LF, and strict calendars then refuse the file.\n12\t */\n13\tconst ENCODED_ICALENDAR_LINE_SEPARATOR = '%0D%0A';\n14\t\n15\t/**\n16\t * The CRLF pair itself, for a calendar which is served as a file rather than carried in a url\n17\t *\n18\t * Note: It is built from its character codes for the very same reason the encoded separator exists - a plain `\\r\\n`\n19\t *       written in the source does not survive the build.\n20\t */\n21\tconst ICALENDAR_LINE_SEPARATOR = String.fromCharCode(13, 10);\n22\t\n23\t/**\n24\t * Where Google Calendar receives what a visitor wants to keep\n25\t */\n26\tconst GOOGLE_CALENDAR_EVENT_URL = 'https://calendar.google.com/calendar/render';\n27\tconst GOOGLE_CALENDAR_SUBSCRIPTION_URL = 'https://calendar.google.com/calendar/r';\n28\t\n29\t/**\n30\t * Protocols of the address of a published calendar\n31\t *\n32\t * Note: A calendar application subscribes to `webcal:`, which is the very same address as its `https:` one. Handing\n33\t *       it out that way is what makes a click subscribe to the calendar instead of downloading it once.\n34\t */\n35\tconst WEBCAL_PROTOCOL = 'webcal:';\n36\t\n37\t/**\n38\t * One event a visitor can put into their calendar\n39\t */\n40\texport type CalendarEvent = {\n41\t    /**\n42\t     * Stable identity of the event, so that a calendar updates the event it already knows instead of adding another one\n43\t     *\n44\t     * Note: When it is missing, the moment the event starts identifies it.\n45\t     */\n46\t    readonly id?: string;\n47\t\n48\t    /**\n49\t     * Headline of the event shown in the calendar\n50\t     */\n51\t    readonly title: string;\n52\t\n53\t    /**\n54\t     * Details of the event shown in the calendar\n55\t     */\n56\t    readonly description: string;\n57\t\n58\t    /**\n59\t     * Moment the event starts, as an ISO 8601 string including the time zone offset\n60\t     */\n61\t    readonly startsAt: string;\n62\t\n63\t    /**\n64\t     * Moment the event ends, as an ISO 8601 string including the time zone offset\n65\t     */\n66\t    readonly endsAt: string;\n67\t\n68\t    /**\n69\t     * Absolute url of the page the event was created from\n70\t     */\n71\t    readonly url: string;\n72\t};\n73\t\n74\t/**\n75\t * Ways of putting one event into a calendar\n76\t */\n77\texport type CalendarLinks = {\n78\t    /**\n79\t     * Url opening the event prefilled in Google Calendar\n80\t     */\n81\t    readonly googleCalendarUrl: string;\n82\t\n83\t    /**\n84\t     * Data url of an iCalendar file for Apple Calendar, Outlook and the rest\n85\t     */\n86\t    readonly icalendarDataUrl: string;\n87\t};\n88\t\n89\t/**\n90\t * Formats a moment as the basic UTC timestamp both Google Calendar and the iCalendar format understand\n91\t *\n92\t * @param isoDateTime ISO 8601 string including the time zone offset\n93\t * @returns timestamp such as `20260820T170000Z`\n94\t */\n95\tfunction formatUtcTimestamp(isoDateTime: string): string {\n96\t    return new Date(isoDateTime).toISOString().replace(/[-:]/g, '').replace(/\\.\\d{3}Z$/, 'Z');\n97\t}\n98\t\n99\t/**\n100\t * Escapes the characters which carry a special meaning inside an iCalendar text value\n101\t *\n102\t * @see https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5545#section-3.3.11\n103\t */\n104\tfunction escapeIcalendarText(text: string): string {\n105\t    return text.replace(/[\\\\;,]/g, (character) => `\\\\${character}`).replace(/\\n/g, '\\\\n');\n106\t}\n107\t\n108\t/**\n109\t * Joins the details of an event with its url, so that the link stays reachable in every calendar which shows only the\n110\t * description of an event\n111\t */\n112\tfunction createEventDetails(event: CalendarEvent): string {\n113\t    return `${event.description}\\n\\n${event.url}`;\n114\t}\n115\t\n116\t/**\n117\t * Builds the url opening the event prefilled in Google Calendar\n118\t */\n119\tfunction createGoogleCalendarUrl(event: CalendarEvent): string {\n120\t    const parameters = new URLSearchParams({\n121\t        action: 'TEMPLATE',\n122\t        text: event.title,\n123\t        dates: `${formatUtcTimestamp(event.startsAt)}/${formatUtcTimestamp(event.endsAt)}`,\n124\t        details: createEventDetails(event),\n125\t        location: event.url,\n126\t    });\n127\t\n128\t    return `${GOOGLE_CALENDAR_EVENT_URL}?${parameters.toString()}`;\n129\t}\n130\t\n131\t/**\n132\t * The lines describing one event inside a calendar\n133\t *\n134\t * Note: The event start doubles as the creation timestamp on purpose - a real timestamp would differ between the server\n135\t *       and the browser render and break the React hydration of the link.\n136\t */\n137\tfunction createIcalendarEventLines(event: CalendarEvent): readonly string[] {\n138\t    const startTimestamp = formatUtcTimestamp(event.startsAt);\n139\t\n140\t    return [\n141\t        'BEGIN:VEVENT',\n142\t        `UID:${event.id ?? startTimestamp}@${new URL(event.url).hostname}`,\n143\t        `DTSTAMP:${startTimestamp}`,\n144\t        `DTSTART:${startTimestamp}`,\n145\t        `DTEND:${formatUtcTimestamp(event.endsAt)}`,\n146\t        `SUMMARY:${escapeIcalendarText(event.title)}`,\n147\t        `DESCRIPTION:${escapeIcalendarText(createEventDetails(event))}`,\n148\t        `LOCATION:${escapeIcalendarText(event.url)}`,\n149\t        `URL:${escapeIcalendarText(event.url)}`,\n150\t        'END:VEVENT',\n151\t    ];\n152\t}\n153\t\n154\t/**\n155\t * The whole content of an iCalendar file, whether it carries one event or every event of a published calendar\n156\t *\n157\t * @param events events the calendar consists of, which a calendar nothing is published in may have none of\n158\t * @param calendarName how a calendar application names the subscription in its own list of calendars\n159\t */\n160\texport function createIcalendarContent(events: readonly CalendarEvent[], calendarName?: string): string {\n161\t    const calendarNameLines = calendarName === undefined ? [] : [`X-WR-CALNAME:${escapeIcalendarText(calendarName)}`];\n162\t\n163\t    return [\n164\t        'BEGIN:VCALENDAR',\n165\t        'VERSION:2.0',\n166\t        `PRODID:${ICALENDAR_PRODUCT_ID}`,\n167\t        'CALSCALE:GREGORIAN',\n168\t        'METHOD:PUBLISH',\n169\t        ...calendarNameLines,\n170\t        ...events.flatMap(createIcalendarEventLines),\n171\t        'END:VCALENDAR',\n172\t        '',\n173\t    ].join(ICALENDAR_LINE_SEPARATOR);\n174\t}\n175\t\n176\t/**\n177\t * Builds the data url of an iCalendar file describing the event\n178\t */\n179\tfunction createIcalendarDataUrl(event: CalendarEvent): string {\n180\t    return `data:text/calendar;charset=utf-8,${createIcalendarContent([event])\n181\t        .split(ICALENDAR_LINE_SEPARATOR)\n182\t        .map((line) => encodeURIComponent(line))\n183\t        .join(ENCODED_ICALENDAR_LINE_SEPARATOR)}`;\n184\t}\n185\t\n186\t/**\n187\t * Turns one event into the links which let a visitor put it into their calendar\n188\t *\n189\t * @param event event to be added into a calendar\n190\t * @returns links for Google Calendar and for every calendar which reads iCalendar files\n191\t */\n192\texport function createCalendarLinks(event: CalendarEvent): CalendarLinks {\n193\t    return {\n194\t        googleCalendarUrl: createGoogleCalendarUrl(event),\n195\t        icalendarDataUrl: createIcalendarDataUrl(event),\n196\t    };\n197\t}\n198\t\n199\t/**\n200\t * Ways of subscribing to a whole published calendar, so that every term it will ever carry arrives on its own\n201\t */\n202\texport type CalendarSubscriptionLinks = * Product identifier announced in the generated iCalendar file\n */\nconst ICALENDAR_PRODUCT_ID = '-//Promptbook//Landing page//CS';\n\n/**\n * Percent encoded CRLF pair which the iCalendar format requires between its lines\n *\n * Note: The separator is kept in its encoded form on purpose. A plain `\\r\\n` string does not survive the build - the\n *       minifier is free to fold it into a template literal, where the language specification normalizes it down to a\n *       bare LF, and strict calendars then refuse the file.\n */\nconst ENCODED_ICALENDAR_LINE_SEPARATOR = '%0D%0A';\n\n/**\n * The CRLF pair itself, for a calendar which is served as a file rather than carried in a url\n *\n * Note: It is built from its character codes for the very same reason the encoded separator exists - a plain `\\r\\n`\n *       written in the source does not survive the build.\n */\nconst ICALENDAR_LINE_SEPARATOR = String.fromCharCode(13, 10);\n\n/**\n * Where Google Calendar receives what a visitor wants to keep\n */\nconst GOOGLE_CALENDAR_EVENT_URL = 'https://calendar.google.com/calendar/render';\nconst GOOGLE_CALENDAR_SUBSCRIPTION_URL = 'https://calendar.google.com/calendar/r';\n\n/**\n * Protocols of the address of a published calendar\n *\n * Note: A calendar application subscribes to `webcal:`, which is the very same address as its `https:` one. Handing\n *       it out that way is what makes a click subscribe to the calendar instead of downloading it once.\n */\nconst WEBCAL_PROTOCOL = 'webcal:';\n\n/**\n * One event a visitor can put into their calendar\n */\nexport type CalendarEvent = {\n    /**\n     * Stable identity of the event, so that a calendar updates the event it already knows instead of adding another one\n     *\n     * Note: When it is missing, the moment the event starts identifies it.\n     */\n    readonly id?: string;\n\n    /**\n     * Headline of the event shown in the calendar\n     */\n    readonly title: string;\n\n    /**\n     * Details of the event shown in the calendar\n     */\n    readonly description: string;\n\n    /**\n     * Moment the event starts, as an ISO 8601 string including the time zone offset\n     */\n    readonly startsAt: string;\n\n    /**\n     * Moment the event ends, as an ISO 8601 string including the time zone offset\n     */\n    readonly endsAt: string;\n\n    /**\n     * Absolute url of the page the event was created from\n     */\n    readonly url: string;\n};\n\n/**\n * Ways of putting one event into a calendar\n */\nexport type CalendarLinks = {\n    /**\n     * Url opening the event prefilled in Google Calendar\n     */\n    readonly googleCalendarUrl: string;\n\n    /**\n     * Data url of an iCalendar file for Apple Calendar, Outlook and the rest\n     */\n    readonly icalendarDataUrl: string;\n};\n\n/**\n * Formats a moment as the basic UTC timestamp both Google Calendar and the iCalendar format understand\n *\n * @param isoDateTime ISO 8601 string including the time zone offset\n * @returns timestamp such as `20260820T170000Z`\n */\nfunction formatUtcTimestamp(isoDateTime: string): string {\n    return new Date(isoDateTime).toISOString().replace(/[-:]/g, '').replace(/\\.\\d{3}Z$/, 'Z');\n}\n\n/**\n * Escapes the characters which carry a special meaning inside an iCalendar text value\n *\n * @see https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5545#section-3.3.11\n */\nfunction escapeIcalendarText(text: string): string {\n    return text.replace(/[\\\\;,]/g, (character) => `\\\\${character}`).replace(/\\n/g, '\\\\n');\n}\n\n/**\n * Joins the details of an event with its url, so that the link stays reachable in every calendar which shows only the\n * description of an event\n */\nfunction createEventDetails(event: CalendarEvent): string {\n    return `${event.description}\\n\\n${event.url}`;\n}\n\n/**\n * Builds the url opening the event prefilled in Google Calendar\n */\nfunction createGoogleCalendarUrl(event: CalendarEvent): string {\n    const parameters = new URLSearchParams({\n        action: 'TEMPLATE',\n        text: event.title,\n        dates: `${formatUtcTimestamp(event.startsAt)}/${formatUtcTimestamp(event.endsAt)}`,\n        details: createEventDetails(event),\n        location: event.url,\n    });\n\n    return `${GOOGLE_CALENDAR_EVENT_URL}?${parameters.toString()}`;\n}\n\n/**\n * The lines describing one event inside a calendar\n *\n * Note: The event start doubles as the creation timestamp on purpose - a real timestamp would differ between the server\n *       and the browser render and break the React hydration of the link.\n */\nfunction createIcalendarEventLines(event: CalendarEvent): readonly string[] {\n    const startTimestamp = formatUtcTimestamp(event.startsAt);\n\n    return [\n        'BEGIN:VEVENT',\n        `UID:${event.id ?? startTimestamp}@${new URL(event.url).hostname}`,\n        `DTSTAMP:${startTimestamp}`,\n        `DTSTART:${startTimestamp}`,\n        `DTEND:${formatUtcTimestamp(event.endsAt)}`,\n        `SUMMARY:${escapeIcalendarText(event.title)}`,\n        `DESCRIPTION:${escapeIcalendarText(createEventDetails(event))}`,\n        `LOCATION:${escapeIcalendarText(event.url)}`,\n        `URL:${escapeIcalendarText(event.url)}`,\n        'END:VEVENT',\n    ];\n}\n\n/**\n * The whole content of an iCalendar file, whether it carries one event or every event of a published calendar\n *\n * @param events events the calendar consists of, which a calendar nothing is published in may have none of\n * @param calendarName how a calendar application names the subscription in its own list of calendars\n */\nexport function createIcalendarContent(events: readonly CalendarEvent[], calendarName?: string): string {\n    const calendarNameLines = calendarName === undefined ? [] : [`X-WR-CALNAME:${escapeIcalendarText(calendarName)}`];\n\n    return [\n        'BEGIN:VCALENDAR',\n        'VERSION:2.0',\n        `PRODID:${ICALENDAR_PRODUCT_ID}`,\n        'CALSCALE:GREGORIAN',\n        'METHOD:PUBLISH',\n        ...calendarNameLines,\n        ...events.flatMap(createIcalendarEventLines),\n        'END:VCALENDAR',\n        '',\n    ].join(ICALENDAR_LINE_SEPARATOR);\n}\n\n/**\n * Builds the data url of an iCalendar file describing the event\n */\nfunction createIcalendarDataUrl(event: CalendarEvent): string {\n    return `data:text/calendar;charset=utf-8,${createIcalendarContent([event])\n        .split(ICALENDAR_LINE_SEPARATOR)\n        .map((line) => encodeURIComponent(line))\n        .join(ENCODED_ICALENDAR_LINE_SEPARATOR)}`;\n}\n\n/**\n * Turns one event into the links which let a visitor put it into their calendar\n *\n * @param event event to be added into a calendar\n * @returns links for Google Calendar and for every calendar which reads iCalendar files\n */\nexport function createCalendarLinks(event: CalendarEvent): CalendarLinks {\n    return {\n        googleCalendarUrl: createGoogleCalendarUrl(event),\n        icalendarDataUrl: createIcalendarDataUrl(event),\n    };\n}\n\n/**\n * Ways of subscribing to a whole published calendar, so that every term it will ever carry arrives on its own\n */\nexport type CalendarSubscriptionLinks = {\n    /**\n     * Url which offers the calendar to Google Calendar\n     */\n    readonly googleCalendarUrl: string;\n\n    /**\n     * Url which offers the calendar to Apple Calendar, Outlook and every other calendar application of a device\n     */\n    readonly webcalUrl: string;\n};\n\n/**\n * Turns the address of a published calendar into the links which subscribe to it\n *\n * @param calendarFeedUrl absolute `https:` url the calendar is served from\n */\nexport function createCalendarSubscriptionLinks(calendarFeedUrl: string): CalendarSubscriptionLinks {\n    const calendarUrl = new URL(calendarFeedUrl);\n    const webcalUrl = `${WEBCAL_PROTOCOL}//${calendarUrl.host}${calendarUrl.pathname}${calendarUrl.search}`;\n    const parameters = new URLSearchParams({ cid: webcalUrl });\n\n    return {\n        googleCalendarUrl: `${GOOGLE_CALENDAR_SUBSCRIPTION_URL}?${parameters.toString()}`,\n        webcalUrl,\n    };\n}\n\n/**\n * Names an iCalendar file after what it describes\n */\nexport function createCalendarFileName(calendarIdentifier: string): string {\n    return `${calendarIdentifier}.ics`;\n}\n","numLines":236,"startLine":1,"totalLines":236}}}

An `inline` one is the very same words as one flowing excerpt, because the card a term is chosen with\n *       is a single button: block elements and destinations inside a button are neither valid nor clickable, and the\n *       compact card cuts the excerpt off after two lines anyway. Both read the same Markdown, so a term is never\n *       described in two different ways — only at two different lengths.\n */\nexport const EVENT_DESCRIPTION_SHAPES = ['block', 'inline'] as const;\n\nexport type EventDescriptionShape = (typeof EVENT_DESCRIPTION_SHAPES)[number];\n\n/**\n * Protocols a description may lead out to, which leaves `javascript:` and `data:` addresses as plain labels\n */\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_ALLOWED_LINK_PROTOCOLS = new Set(['https:', 'http:', 'mailto:']);\n\n/**\n * What an excerpt puts between two blocks of the description and in front of each item of a list\n */\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_BLOCK_SEPARATOR = ' ';\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_LIST_ITEM_MARKER = '• ';\n\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME = 'font-mono text-[0.95em]';\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME = 'mt-3 first:mt-0';\n\n/**\n * The address of a link which may be opened, or `null` for one which stays a label\n *\n * Note: A site-relative address is kept as it was written, because a description has no page of its own to resolve it\n *       against. A protocol-relative `//host` one is refused, so it can never leave the site unnoticed.\n */\nfunction resolveEventDescriptionHref(href: string): string | null {\n    if (href.startsWith('/')) {\n        return href.startsWith('//') ? null : href;\n    }\n\n    try {\n        const url = new URL(href);\n\n        return EVENT_DESCRIPTION_ALLOWED_LINK_PROTOCOLS.has(url.protocol) ? url.href : null;\n    } catch {\n        // An address which is not an address at all remains readable as a label.\n        return null;\n    }\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionLink(token: Tokens.Link, shape: EventDescriptionShape): ReactNode {\n    const label = renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape);\n    const href = resolveEventDescriptionHref(token.href);\n\n    if (shape === 'inline' || href === null) {\n        return label;\n    }\n\n    // Note: A description is read on the way into a room, so its links open beside it rather than taking a\n    //       participant out of the door they are standing in.\n    return (\n        <a\n            href={href}\n            target=\"_blank\"\n            rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\n            className=\"font-semibold text-room-accent underline decoration-room-accent/50 underline-offset-2 transition hover:text-room-heading\"\n        >\n            {label}\n        </a>\n    );\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionInlineToken(token: MarkedToken, shape: EventDescriptionShape): ReactNode {\n    switch (token.type) {\n        case 'strong':\n            return <strong className=\"font-semibold\">{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</strong>;\n        case 'em':\n            return <em>{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</em>;\n        case 'del':\n            return <del>{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</del>;\n        case 'codespan':\n            return <code className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME}>{token.text}</code>;\n        case 'br':\n            return shape === 'inline' ? EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_BLOCK_SEPARATOR : <br />;\n        case 'link':\n            return renderEventDescriptionLink(token, shape);\n        case 'image':\n            // A description is a passage of text rather than a gallery, so an image is read by what it was called.\n            return readMarkdownTokenText(token) || token.href;\n        case 'text':\n            return token.tokens === undefined\n                ? readMarkdownTokenText(token)\n                : renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape);\n        default:\n            // Raw HTML and anything else only ever contributes its text, so a description can carry no markup of its own.\n            return readMarkdownTokenText(token);\n    }\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(\n    tokens: readonly Token[],\n    shape: EventDescriptionShape,\n): readonly ReactNode[] {\n    return tokens.map((token, index) => (\n        <Fragment key={`${token.type}-${index}`}>\n            {renderEventDescriptionInlineToken(token as MarkedToken, shape)}\n        </Fragment>\n    ));\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(tokens: readonly Token[]): readonly ReactNode[] {\n    return tokens.flatMap((token, index): readonly ReactNode[] => {\n        const markdownToken = token as MarkedToken;\n        const key = `${markdownToken.type}-${index}`;\n\n        switch (markdownToken.type) {\n            case 'space':\n            case 'def':\n                return [];\n            case 'heading':\n                // Note: A description is one passage rather than a document of its own, so an authored heading leads\n                //       its paragraph instead of claiming a level in the outline of the page around it.\n                return [\n                    <p key={key} className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} font-semibold`}>\n                        {renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(markdownToken.tokens, 'block')}\n                    </p>,\n                ];\n            case 'list': {\n                const items = markdownToken.items.map((item, itemIndex) => (\n                    <li key={`item-${itemIndex}`}>{renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(item.tokens)}</li>\n                ));\n\n                return [\n                    markdownToken.ordered ? (\n                        <ol\n                            key={key}\n                            start={Number(markdownToken.start) || 1}\n                            className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} list-decimal space-y-1 pl-5`}\n                        >\n                            {items}\n                        </ol>\n                    ) : (\n                        <ul key={key} className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} list-disc space-y-1 pl-5`}>\n                            {items}\n                        </ul>\n                    ),\n                ];\n            }\n            case 'blockquote':\n                return [\n                    <blockquote\n                        key={key}\n                        className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} border-l-2 border-room-border/20 pl-3 italic`}\n                    >\n                        {renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(markdownToken.tokens)}\n                    </blockquote>,\n                ];\n            case 'code':\n                return [\n                    <pre\n             <code className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME}>{markdownToken.text}</code>\n                    </pre>,\n                ];\n            case 'hr':\n                return [<hr key={key} className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} border-room-border/20`} />];\n            case 'table':\n                return [\n                    <table key={key} </thead>\n                        <tbody>\n                            {markdownToken.rows.map((row, rowIndex) => (\n                                <tr key={`row-${rowIndex}`}>\n {renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(cell.tokens, 'block')}\n                                        </td>\n                                    ))}\n                                </tr>\n (readonly ReactNode[])[] {\n    return tokens.flatMap((token): readonly (readonly ReactNode[])[] => {\n        const markdownToken = token as MarkedToken;\n\n        switch (markdownToken.type) {\n className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME}>{markdownToken.text}</code>]];\n            case 'table':\n                return [markdownToken.header, ...markdownToken.rows].map((row) =>\n 'text-cyan-600',\n    },\n    room: {\n        card: 'border-room-border/10 bg-room-overlay/[0.04] hover:border-room-accent/40',\n        selectedCard: 'border-room-accent/70 bg-room-accent/10 ring-2 ring-room-accent/20',\n        heading: 'text-room-heading',\n        title: 'text-room-heading',\n        description: 'text-room-text',\n        formatBadge: 'bg-room-overlay/10 text-room-text',\n        price: 'text-room-text',\n        note: 'text-room-text',\n        noteIcon: 'text-room-accent',\n    },\n};\n\n/**\n * The two amounts of room a term is given: the full card a visitor chooses a readonly heading: string;\n            readonly title: string;\n            readonly description: string;\n            readonly detailsRow: string;\n            readonly formatBadge: string;\n text-xs leading-5',\n        detailsRow: 'mt-1.5 gap-1.5 text-xs',\n        formatBadge: 'px-2 py-0.5 text-[11px]',\n        note: 'mt-1.5 gap-1.5 text-xs',\n        noteIcon: 'h-3.5 w-3.5',\n    },\n};\n\ntype EventTermOptionCardProps = {\n    readonly occurrence: EventOccurrence;\n    readonly isSelected: boolean;\n    readonly onSelect: () => void;\n\n    /**\n     * Moment the server built the page this card is offered on at, which is what makes this term today, tomorrow, or\n     * one of the days of this week\n     *\n     * Note: That moment comes from the server rather than from the browser, so the card says the very same thing it\n     *       was sent as instead of renaming its day the instant it hydrates.\n     */\n    readonly currentTime: string;\n\n    /**\n     * Whether the card says what this very term is about\n     *\n     * Note: An event whose terms each have a subject of their own is chosen by that subject, so those cards name it.\n     *       An event which is the very same workshop held in another form or on another day is chosen by when and\n     *       where it is, and naming it again on every card would only repeat what the card already carries.\n     */\n    readonly isTopicShown?: boolean;\n\n    /**\n     * Which of the two surfaces this card is offered on, see `EVENT_TERM_OPTION_CARD_APPEARANCES`\n     */\n    readonly appearance?: formatBadge: 'bg-room-overlay/10 text-room-text',\n        price: 'text-room-text',\n        note: 'text-room-text',\n        noteIcon: 'text-room-accent',\n    },\n};\n\n/**\n * The two amounts of room a term is given: the full card a visitor chooses a term with, and the tighter one a surface\n * which is already about one term offers the other terms beside it with\n */\nexport const EVENT_TERM_DENSITIES = ['comfortable', 'compact'] as const;\n\nexport type EventTermDensity = (typeof EVENT_TERM_DENSITIES)[number];\n\n/**\n * How much room each part of one card takes at each of those densities\n *\n * Note: A compact card says everything a comfortable one says, in the same order, only quieter and with a description\n *       which is cut off after two lines — so a term offered beside another one is never described differently, merely\n *       shorter.\n */\nconst EVENT_TERM_OPTION_CARD_DENSITIES: Readonly<\n    Record<\n        EventTermDensity,\n        {\n            readonly card: string;\n            readonly heading: string;\n            readonly title: string;\n            readonly description: string;\n            readonly detailsRow: string;\n            readonly formatBadge: string;\n            readonly note: string;\n            readonly noteIcon: string;\n        }\n    >\n> = {\n    comfortable: {\n        card: 'rounded-xl p-4',\n        heading: 'text-lg',\n        title: 'mt-2 block text-base',\n        description: 'mt-1 block text-sm leading-relaxed',\n        detailsRow: 'mt-2 gap-2 text-sm',\n        formatBadge: 'px-2.5 py-1 text-xs',\n        note: 'mt-2 gap-2 text-sm',\n        noteIcon: 'h-4 w-4',\n    },\n    compact: {\n        card: 'rounded-lg p-3',\n        heading: 'text-base',\n        title: 'mt-1 block text-sm',\n        description: 'mt-0.5 line-clamp-2 text-xs leading-5',\n        detailsRow: 'mt-1.5 gap-1.5 text-xs',\n        formatBadge: 'px-2 py-0.5 text-[11px]',\n        note: 'mt-1.5 gap-1.5 text-xs',\n        noteIcon: 'h-3.5 w-3.5',\n    },\n};\n\ntype EventTermOptionCardProps = {\n    readonly occurrence: EventOccurrence;\n    readonly isSelected: boolean;\n    readonly onSelect: () => void;\n\n    /**\n     * Moment the server built the page this card is offered on at, which is what makes this term today, tomorrow, or\n     * one of the days of this week\n     *\n     * Note: That moment comes from the server rather than from the browser, so the card says the very same thing it\n     *       was sent as instead of renaming its day the instant it hydrates.\n     */\n    readonly currentTime: string;\n\n    /**\n     * Whether the card says what this very term is about\n     *\n     * Note: An event whose terms each have a subject of their own is chosen by that subject, so those cards name it.\n     *       An event which is the very same workshop held in another form or on another day is chosen by when and\n     *       where it is, and naming it again on every card would only repeat what the card already carries.\n     */\n    readonly isTopicShown?: boolean;\n\n    /**\n     * Which of the two surfaces this card is offered on, see `EVENT_TERM_OPTION_CARD_APPEARANCES`\n     */\n    readonly appearance?: EventTermAppearance;\n\n    /**\n     * How much room this card is given, see `EVENT_TERM_OPTION_CARD_DENSITIES`\n     */\n    readonly density?: EventTermDensity;\n\n    /**\n     * Icon and text of the one line each landing page adds about its terms, such as how long they take or how many\n     * seats are left in them\n     */\n    readonly noteIcon: LucideIcon;\n    readonly noteText: string;\n};\n\n/**\n * One term of an event as a visitor picks it, which says when it is held, what it is about, in what form, and at different ways. What only one of those pages knows about\n *       its terms is said in the note beneath.\n */\nexport function EventTermOptionCard({\n    occurrence,\n    isSelected,\n    onSelect,\n    currentTime,\n    isTopicShown = false,\n    appearance = 'light',\n    density = 'comfortable',\n    noteIcon: NoteIcon,\n    noteText,\n}: EventTermOptionCardProps) {\n    const appearanceClassNames = EVENT_TERM_OPTION_CARD_APPEARANCES[appearance];\n    const densityClassNames = EVENT_TERM_OPTION_CARD_DENSITIES[density];\n    const phase = getWorkshopPhase(occurrence, Date.parse(currentTime));\n    const isWorkshopStartingSoon = isWorkshopPhaseUpcoming(phase) && phase !== 'upcoming';\n\n    return (\n        <button\n            type=\"button\"\n            aria-pressed={isSelected}\n            onClick={onSelect}\n            className={cn(\n                'border text-left transition-all',\n                densityClassNames.card,\n                isSelected ? appearanceClassNames.selectedCard : appearanceClassNames.card,\n            )}\n        >\n            <span\n                className={cn(\n                    'flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2 font-bold',\n                    densityClassNames.heading,\n                    appearanceClassNames.heading,\n                )}\n            >\n                <span>\n                    {formatCzechWorkshopRelativeDay(occurrence.startsAt, currentTime)} ·{' '}\n                    {formatCzechWorkshopTimeRange(occurrence.startsAt, occurrence.endsAt)}\n                </span>\n                {isWorkshopStartingSoon && (\n                    <WorkshopPhaseBadge\n                        phase={phase}\n                        tone={appearance}\n                        className={density === 'compact' ? '!px-2 !py-0.5 !text-[11px]' : undefined}\n                    />\n                )}\n            </span>\n            {isTopicShown && (\n                <>\n                    <span className={cn('font-semibold', densityClassNames.title, appearanceClassNames.title)}>\n                        {occurrence.title}\n                    </span>\n                    {occurrence.description.trim() !== '' && (\n                        <EventDescription\n                            description={occurrence.description}\n                            shape=\"inline\"\n        <span className={cn('flex flex-wrap items-center', densityClassNames.detailsRow)}>\n                <span\n                    className={cn(\n                        'rounded-full {formatEventFormat(occurrence.event)}\n                </span>\n                <span className={cn('font-medium', appearanceClassNames.price)}>\n                    {formatEventPrice(occurrence.event.priceCzk)}\n                </span>\n            </span>\n            <span className={cn('flex items-center', densityClassNames.note, appearanceClassNames.note)}>\n placeholder:text-room-subtle\"\n                                aria-invalid={isValidationVisible && !isEmailValid}\n                            />\n                            {isValidationVisible && className={WORKSHOP_CONNECTION_DESCRIPTION_CLASS_NAME}\n                        />\n                    ) : (\n                        <p
