An `inline` one is the very same words as one flowing excerpt, because the card a term is chosen with\n *       is a single button: block elements and destinations inside a button are neither valid nor clickable, and the\n *       compact card cuts the excerpt off after two lines anyway. Both read the same Markdown, so a term is never\n *       described in two different ways — only at two different lengths.\n */\nexport const EVENT_DESCRIPTION_SHAPES = ['block', 'inline'] as const;\n\nexport type EventDescriptionShape = (typeof EVENT_DESCRIPTION_SHAPES)[number];\n\n/**\n * Protocols a description may lead out to, which leaves `javascript:` and `data:` addresses as plain labels\n */\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_ALLOWED_LINK_PROTOCOLS = new Set(['https:', 'http:', 'mailto:']);\n\n/**\n * What an excerpt puts between two blocks of the description and in front of each item of a list\n */\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_BLOCK_SEPARATOR = ' ';\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_LIST_ITEM_MARKER = '• ';\n\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME = 'font-mono text-[0.95em]';\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME = 'mt-3 first:mt-0';\n\n/**\n * The address of a link which may be opened, or `null` for one which stays a label\n *\n * Note: A site-relative address is kept as it was written, because a description has no page of its own to resolve it\n *       against. A protocol-relative `//host` one is refused, so it can never leave the site unnoticed.\n */\nfunction resolveEventDescriptionHref(href: string): string | null {\n    if (href.startsWith('/')) {\n        return href.startsWith('//') ? null : href;\n    }\n\n    try {\n        const url = new URL(href);\n\n        return EVENT_DESCRIPTION_ALLOWED_LINK_PROTOCOLS.has(url.protocol) ? url.href : null;\n    } catch {\n        // An address which is not an address at all remains readable as a label.\n        return null;\n    }\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionLink(token: Tokens.Link, shape: EventDescriptionShape): ReactNode {\n    const label = renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape);\n    const href = resolveEventDescriptionHref(token.href);\n\n    if (shape === 'inline' || href === null) {\n        return label;\n    }\n\n    // Note: A description is read on the way into a room, so its links open beside it rather than taking a\n    //       participant out of the door they are standing in.\n    return (\n        <a\n            href={href}\n            target=\"_blank\"\n            rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\n            className=\"font-semibold text-room-accent underline decoration-room-accent/50 underline-offset-2 transition hover:text-room-heading\"\n        >\n            {label}\n        </a>\n    );\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionInlineToken(token: MarkedToken, shape: EventDescriptionShape): ReactNode {\n    switch (token.type) {\n        case 'strong':\n            return <strong className=\"font-semibold\">{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</strong>;\n        case 'em':\n            return <em>{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</em>;\n        case 'del':\n            return <del>{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</del>;\n        case 'codespan':\n            return <code className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME}>{token.text}</code>;\n        case 'br':\n            return shape === 'inline' ? EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_BLOCK_SEPARATOR : <br />;\n        case 'link':\n            return renderEventDescriptionLink(token, shape);\n        case 'image':\n            // A description is a passage of text rather than a gallery, so an image is read by what it was called.\n            return readMarkdownTokenText(token) || token.href;\n        case 'text':\n            return token.tokens === undefined\n                ? readMarkdownTokenText(token)\n                : renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape);\n        default:\n            // Raw HTML and anything else only ever contributes its text, so a description can carry no markup of its own.\n            return readMarkdownTokenText(token);\n    }\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(\n    tokens: readonly Token[],\n    shape: EventDescriptionShape,\n): readonly ReactNode[] {\n    return tokens.map((token, index) => (\n        <Fragment key={`${token.type}-${index}`}>\n            {renderEventDescriptionInlineToken(token as MarkedToken, shape)}\n        </Fragment>\n    ));\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(tokens: readonly Token[]): readonly ReactNode[] {\n    return tokens.flatMap((token, index): readonly ReactNode[] => {\n        const markdownToken = token as MarkedToken;\n        const key = `${markdownToken.type}-${index}`;\n\n        switch (markdownToken.type) {\n            case 'space':\n            case 'def':\n                return [];\n            case 'heading':\n                // Note: A description is one passage rather than a document of its own, so an authored heading leads\n                //       its paragraph instead of claiming a level in the outline of the page around it.\n                return [\n                    <p key={key} className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} font-semibold`}>\n                        {renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(markdownToken.tokens, 'block')}\n                    </p>,\n                ];\n            case 'list': {\n                const items = markdownToken.items.map((item, itemIndex) => (\n                    <li key={`item-${itemIndex}`}>{renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(item.tokens)}</li>\n                ));\n\n                return [\n                    markdownToken.ordered ? (\n                        <ol\n                            key={key}\n                            start={Number(markdownToken.start) || 1}\n                            className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} list-decimal space-y-1 pl-5`}\n                        >\n                            {items}\n                        </ol>\n                    ) : (\n                        <ul key={key} className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} list-disc space-y-1 pl-5`}>\n                            {items}\n                        </ul>\n                    ),\n                ];\n            }\n            case 'blockquote':\n                return [\n                    <blockquote\n                        key={key}\n                        className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} border-l-2 border-room-border/20 pl-3 italic`}\n                    >\n                        {renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(markdownToken.tokens)}\n                    </blockquote>,\n                ];\n            case 'code':\n                return [\n                    <pre\n                        key={key}\n                        className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} max-w-full overflow-x-auto rounded bg-room-overlay/[0.06] p-2`}\n                    >\n                        <code className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME}>{markdownToken.text}</code>\n                    </pre>,\n                ];\n            case 'hr':\n                return [<hr key={key} className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} border-room-border/20`} />];\n            case 'table':\n                return [\n                    <table key={key} className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} block max-w-full overflow-x-auto`}>\n                        <thead>\n                            <tr>\n                                {markdownToken.header.map((cell, cellIndex) => (\n                                    <th key={`header-${cellIndex}`} className=\"pr-4 text-left font-semibold\">\n                                        {renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(cell.tokens, 'block')}\n                                    </th>\n                                ))}\n                            </tr>\n                        </thead>\n                        <tbody>\n                            {markdownToken.rows.map((row, rowIndex) => (\n                                <tr key={`row-${rowIndex}`}>\n                                    {row.map((cell, cellIndex) => (\n                                        <td key={`cell-${cellIndex}`} className=\"pr-4 align-top\">\n                                            {renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(cell.tokens, 'block')}\n                                        </td>\n                                    ))}\n                                </tr>\n                            ))}\n                        </tbody>\n                    </table>,\n                ];\n            default:\n                return [\n                    <p key={key} className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME}>\n                        {'tokens' in markdownToken && markdownToken.tokens !== undefined\n                            ? renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(markdownToken.tokens, 'block')\n                            : readMarkdownTokenText(markdownToken)}\n                    </p>,\n                ];\n        }\n    });\n}\n\n/**\n * Every block of a description as its own run of inline nodes, in the order it was written\n */\nfunction createEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(tokens: readonly Token[]): readonly (readonly ReactNode[])[] {\n    return tokens.flatMap((token): readonly (readonly ReactNode[])[] => {\n        const markdownToken = token as MarkedToken;\n\n        switch (markdownToken.type) {\n            case 'space':\n            case 'def':\n            case 'hr':\n                return [];\n            case 'blockquote':\n                return createEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(markdownToken.tokens);\n            case 'list':\n                // An excerpt has no bullets to indent, so each item says that it is one.\n                return markdownToken.items.map((item) => [\n                    EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_LIST_ITEM_MARKER,\n                    ...joinEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(createEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(item.tokens)),\n                ]);\n            case 'code':\n                return [[<code key=\"code\" className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME}>{markdownToken.text}</code>]];\n            case 'table':\n                return [markdownToken.header, ...markdownToken.rows].map((row) =>\n                    joinEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(\n                        row.map((cell) => renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(cell.tokens, 'inline')),\n                    ),\n                );\n            default:\n                return [\n                    'tokens' in markdownToken && markdownToken.tokens !== undefined\n                        ? renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(markdownToken.tokens, 'inline')\n                        : [readMarkdownTokenText(markdownToken)],\n                ];\n        }\n    });\n}\n\nfunction joinEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(runs: readonly (readonly ReactNode[])[]): readonly ReactNode[] {\n    return runs.flatMap((run, index) => [\n        ...(index === 0 ? [] : [EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_BLOCK_SEPARATOR]),\n        <Fragment key={`run-${index}`}>{run}</Fragment>,\n    ]);\n}\n\ntype EventDescriptionProps = {\n    /**\n     * The words an administrator wrote about one event, written as Markdown\n     */\n    readonly description: string;\n\n    /**\n     * How much room they are read in, see `EVENT_DESCRIPTION_SHAPES`\n     */\n    readonly shape?: EventDescriptionShape;\n    readonly className?: string;\n};\n\n/**\n * The description of one event, read as the Markdown it was written in\n *\n * Note: This is the one place which decides how an authored description reads, so the door of a room, the card a term\n *       is chosen with and the recap of a workshop can never interpret the same words differently. The description\n *       carries no markup of its own: raw HTML only ever contributes its text, an image is read by its label, and only\n *       an address of a known protocol ever becomes a link.\n * Note: The formatting takes no colours of its own and inherits the ones of the surface it is read on, so the fixed\n *       palette of a landing page and the appearance a member chose for their room both stay intact. What does need a\n *       colour — a link, a quotation, a block of code — only ever appears in the whole passage, which is read inside a\n *       room.\n */\nexport function EventDescription({ description, shape = 'block', className }: EventDescriptionProps) {\n    const tokens = readMarkdownTokens(description);\n\n    if (shape === 'inline') {\n        return <span className={className}>{joinEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(createEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(tokens))}</span>;\n    }\n\n    return <div className={className}>{renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(tokens)}</div>;\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":279,"oldLines":7,"newStart":279,"newLines":11,"lines":["     const tokens = readMarkdownTokens(description);"," ","     if (shape === 'inline') {","-        return <span className={className}>{joinEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(createEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(tokens))}</span>;","+        return (","+            <span className={className}>","+                {joinEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(createEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(tokens))}","+            </span>","+        );","     }"," ","     return <div className={className}>{renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(tokens)}</div>;"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false}}

An `inline` one is the very same words as one flowing excerpt, because the card a term is chosen with\n *       is a single button: block elements and destinations inside a button are neither valid nor clickable, and the\n *       compact card cuts the excerpt off after two lines anyway. Both read the same Markdown, so a term is never\n *       described in two different ways — only at two different lengths.\n */\nexport const EVENT_DESCRIPTION_SHAPES = ['block', 'inline'] as const;\n\nexport type EventDescriptionShape = (typeof EVENT_DESCRIPTION_SHAPES)[number];\n\n/**\n * Protocols a description may lead out to, which leaves `javascript:` and `data:` addresses as plain labels\n */\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_ALLOWED_LINK_PROTOCOLS = new Set(['https:', 'http:', 'mailto:']);\n\n/**\n * What an excerpt puts between two blocks of the description and in front of each item of a list\n */\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_BLOCK_SEPARATOR = ' ';\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_LIST_ITEM_MARKER = '• ';\n\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME = 'font-mono text-[0.95em]';\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME = 'mt-3 first:mt-0';\n\n/**\n * The address of a link which may be opened, or `null` for one which stays a label\n *\n * Note: A site-relative address is kept as it was written, because a description has no page of its own to resolve it\n *       against. A protocol-relative `//host` one is refused, so it can never leave the site unnoticed.\n */\nfunction resolveEventDescriptionHref(href: string): string | null {\n    if (href.startsWith('/')) {\n        return href.startsWith('//') ? null : href;\n    }\n\n    try {\n        const url = new URL(href);\n\n        return EVENT_DESCRIPTION_ALLOWED_LINK_PROTOCOLS.has(url.protocol) ? url.href : null;\n    } catch {\n        // An address which is not an address at all remains readable as a label.\n        return null;\n    }\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionLink(token: Tokens.Link, shape: EventDescriptionShape): ReactNode {\n    const label = renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape);\n    const href = resolveEventDescriptionHref(token.href);\n\n    if (shape === 'inline' || href === null) {\n        return label;\n    }\n\n    // Note: A description is read on the way into a room, so its links open beside it rather than taking a\n    //       participant out of the door they are standing in.\n    return (\n        <a\n            href={href}\n            target=\"_blank\"\n            rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\n            className=\"font-semibold text-room-accent underline decoration-room-accent/50 underline-offset-2 transition hover:text-room-heading\"\n        >\n            {label}\n        </a>\n    );\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionInlineToken(token: MarkedToken, shape: EventDescriptionShape): ReactNode {\n    switch (token.type) {\n        case 'strong':\n            return <strong className=\"font-semibold\">{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</strong>;\n        case 'em':\n            return <em>{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</em>;\n        case 'del':\n            return <del>{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</del>;\n        case 'codespan':\n            return <code className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME}>{token.text}</code>;\n        case 'br':\n            return shape === 'inline' ? (\n                        <ol\n                            key={key}\n                            start={Number(markdownToken.start) || 1}\n                            className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} list-decimal space-y-1 pl-5`}\n                        >\n                            {items}\n                        </ol>\n                    ) : (\n                        <ul key={key} className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} list-disc space-y-1 pl-5`}>\n                            {items}\n                        </ul>\n                    ),\n                ];\n            }\n            case 'blockquote':\n                return [\n                    <blockquote\n                        key={key}\n                        className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} border-l-2 border-room-border/20 pl-3 italic`}\n                    >\n                        {renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(markdownToken.tokens)}\n                    </blockquote>,\n                ];\n            case 'code':\n                return [\n                    <pre\n             <code className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME}>{markdownToken.text}</code>\n                    </pre>,\n                ];\n            case 'hr':\n                return [<hr className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME}>\n                        {'tokens' in markdownToken && markdownToken.tokens !== undefined\n                            ? renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(markdownToken.tokens, 'block')\n                            : readMarkdownTokenText(markdownToken)}\n                    </p>,\n                ];\n        }\n    });\n}\n\n/**\n * Every block of a description as its own run of inline nodes, in the order it was written\n */\nfunction createEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(tokens: readonly Token[]): readonly (readonly ReactNode[])[] {\n    return tokens.flatMap((token): readonly (readonly ReactNode[])[] => {\n        const markdownToken = token as MarkedToken;\n\n        switch (markdownToken.type) {\n            case 'space':\n            case 'def':\n            case 'hr':\n                return [];\n            case 'blockquote':\n                return createEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(markdownToken.tokens);\n            case 'list':\n                // An excerpt has no bullets to indent, so each item says that it is one.\n                return markdownToken.items.map((item) => [\n                    EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_LIST_ITEM_MARKER,\n                    ...joinEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(createEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(item.tokens)),\n                ]);\n            case 'code':\n                return [[<code key=\"code\" className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME}>{markdownToken.text}</code>]];\n            case 'table':\n                return [markdownToken.header, ...markdownToken.rows].map((row) =>\n                    joinEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(\n                        row.map((cell) => renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(cell.tokens, 'inline')),\n                    ),\n                );\n [] : [EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_BLOCK_SEPARATOR]),\n        <Fragment key={`run-${index}`}>{run}</Fragment>,\n    ]);\n}\n\ntype EventDescriptionProps = {\n    /**\n     * The words an administrator wrote about one event, written as Markdown\n     */\n    readonly description: string;\n\n    /**\n     * How much room they are read in, see `EVENT_DESCRIPTION_SHAPES`\n     */\n    readonly shape?: EventDescriptionShape;\n    readonly className?: string;\n};\n\n/**\n * The description of one event, read as the Markdown it was written in\n *\n * Note: This is the one place which decides how an authored description reads, so the door of a room, the card a term\n *       is chosen with and the recap of a workshop can never interpret the same words differently. The description\n *       carries no markup of its own: raw HTML only ever contributes its text, an image is read by its label, and only\n *       an address of a known protocol ever becomes a link.\n * Note: The formatting takes no colours of its own and inherits the ones of the surface it is read on, so the fixed\n *       palette of a landing page and the appearance a member chose for their room both stay intact. An `inline` one is the very same words as one flowing excerpt, because the card a term is chosen with\n *       is a single button: block elements and destinations inside a button are neither valid nor clickable, and the\n *       compact card cuts the excerpt off after two lines anyway. Both read the same Markdown, so a term is never\n *       described in two different ways — only at two different lengths.\n */\nexport const EVENT_DESCRIPTION_SHAPES = ['block', 'inline'] as const;\n\nexport type EventDescriptionShape = (typeof EVENT_DESCRIPTION_SHAPES)[number];\n\n/**\n * Protocols a description may lead out to, which leaves `javascript:` and `data:` addresses as plain labels\n */\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_ALLOWED_LINK_PROTOCOLS = new Set(['https:', 'http:', 'mailto:']);\n\n/**\n * What an excerpt puts between two blocks of the description and in front of each item of a list\n */\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_BLOCK_SEPARATOR = ' ';\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_LIST_ITEM_MARKER = '• ';\n\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME = 'font-mono text-[0.95em]';\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME = 'mt-3 first:mt-0';\n\n/**\n * The address of a link which may be opened, or `null` for one which stays a label\n *\n * Note: A site-relative address is kept as it was written, because a description has no page of its own to resolve it\n *       against. A protocol-relative `//host` one is refused, so it can never leave the site unnoticed.\n */\nfunction resolveEventDescriptionHref(href: string): string | null {\n    if (href.startsWith('/')) {\n        return href.startsWith('//') ? null : href;\n    }\n\n    try {\n        const url = new URL(href);\n\n        return EVENT_DESCRIPTION_ALLOWED_LINK_PROTOCOLS.has(url.protocol) ? url.href : null;\n    } catch {\n        // An address which is not an address at all remains readable as a label.\n        return null;\n    }\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionLink(token: Tokens.Link, shape: EventDescriptionShape): ReactNode {\n    const label = renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape);\n    const href = resolveEventDescriptionHref(token.href);\n\n    if (shape === 'inline' || href === null) {\n        return label;\n    }\n\n    // Note: A description is read on the way into a room, so its links open beside it rather than taking a\n    //       participant out of the door they are standing in.\n    return (\n        <a\n            href={href}\n            target=\"_blank\"\n            rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\n            className=\"font-semibold text-room-accent underline decoration-room-accent/50 underline-offset-2 transition hover:text-room-heading\"\n        >\n            {label}\n        </a>\n    );\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionInlineToken(token: MarkedToken, shape: EventDescriptionShape): ReactNode {\n    switch (token.type) {\n        case 'strong':\n            return <strong className=\"font-semibold\">{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</strong>;\n        case 'em':\n            return <em>{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</em>;\n        case 'del':\n            return <del>{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</del>;\n        case 'codespan':\n            return <code className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME}>{token.text}</code>;\n        case 'br':\n            return shape === 'inline' ? EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_BLOCK_SEPARATOR : <br />;\n        case 'link':\n            return renderEventDescriptionLink(token, shape);\n        case 'image':\n            // A description is a passage of text rather than a gallery, so an image is read by what it was called.\n            return readMarkdownTokenText(token) || token.href;\n        case 'text':\n            return token.tokens === undefined\n                ? readMarkdownTokenText(token)\n                : renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape);\n        default:\n            // Raw HTML and anything else only ever contributes its text, so a description can carry no markup of its own.\n            return readMarkdownTokenText(token);\n    }\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(\n    tokens: readonly Token[],\n    shape: EventDescriptionShape,\n): readonly ReactNode[] {\n    return tokens.map((token, index) => (\n        <Fragment key={`${token.type}-${index}`}>\n            {renderEventDescriptionInlineToken(token as MarkedToken, shape)}\n        </Fragment>\n    ));\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(tokens: readonly Token[]): readonly ReactNode[] {\n    return tokens.flatMap((token, index): readonly ReactNode[] => {\n        const markdownToken = token as MarkedToken;\n        const key = `${markdownToken.type}-${index}`;\n\n        switch (markdownToken.type) {\n            case 'space':\n            case 'def':\n                return [];\n            case 'heading':\n                // Note: A description is one passage rather than a document of its own, so an authored heading leads\n                //       its paragraph instead of claiming a level in the outline of the page around it.\n                return [\n                    <p key={key} className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} font-semibold`}>\n                        {renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(markdownToken.tokens, 'block')}\n                    </p>,\n                ];\n            case 'list': {\n                const items = markdownToken.items.map((item, itemIndex) => (\n                    <li key={`item-${itemIndex}`}>{renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(item.tokens)}</li>\n                ));\n\n                return [\n                    markdownToken.ordered ? (\n                        <ol\n                            key={key}\n                            start={Number(markdownToken.start) || 1}\n                            className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} list-decimal space-y-1 pl-5`}\n                        >\n                            {items}\n                        </ol>\n                    ) : (\n                        <ul key={key} className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} list-disc space-y-1 pl-5`}>\n                            {items}\n                        </ul>\n                    ),\n                ];\n            }\n            case 'blockquote':\n                return [\n                    <blockquote\n                        key={key}\n                        className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} border-l-2 border-room-border/20 pl-3 italic`}\n                    >\n                        {renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(markdownToken.tokens)}\n                    </blockquote>,\n                ];\n            case 'code':\n                return [\n                    <pre\n                        key={key}\n                        className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} max-w-full overflow-x-auto rounded bg-room-overlay/[0.06] p-2`}\n                    >\n                        <code className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME}>{markdownToken.text}</code>\n                    </pre>,\n                ];\n            case 'hr':\n                return [<hr key={key} className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} border-room-border/20`} />];\n            case 'table':\n                return [\n                    <table\n                        key={key}\n                        className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} block max-w-full overflow-x-auto`}\n                    >\n                        <thead>\n                            <tr>\n                                {markdownToken.header.map((cell, cellIndex) => (\n                                    <th key={`header-${cellIndex}`} className=\"pr-4 text-left font-semibold\">\n                                        {renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(cell.tokens, 'block')}\n                                    </th>\n                                ))}\n                            </tr>\n                        </thead>\n                        <tbody>\n                            {markdownToken.rows.map((row, rowIndex) => (\n                                <tr key={`row-${rowIndex}`}>\n                                    {row.map((cell, cellIndex) => (\n                                        <td key={`cell-${cellIndex}`} className=\"pr-4 align-top\">\n                                            {renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(cell.tokens, 'block')}\n                                        </td>\n                                    ))}\n                                </tr>\n                            ))}\n                        </tbody>\n                    </table>,\n                ];\n            default:\n                return [\n                    <p key={key} className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME}>\n                        {'tokens' in markdownToken && markdownToken.tokens !== undefined\n                            ? renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(markdownToken.tokens, 'block')\n                            : readMarkdownTokenText(markdownToken)}\n                    </p>,\n                ];\n        }\n    });\n}\n\n/**\n * Every block of a description as its own run of inline nodes, in the order it was written\n */\nfunction createEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(tokens: readonly Token[]): readonly (readonly ReactNode[])[] {\n    return tokens.flatMap((token): readonly (readonly ReactNode[])[] => {\n        const markdownToken = token as MarkedToken;\n\n        switch (markdownToken.type) {\n            case 'space':\n            case 'def':\n            case 'hr':\n                return [];\n            case 'blockquote':\n                return createEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(markdownToken.tokens);\n            case 'list':\n                // An excerpt has no bullets to indent, so each item says that it is one.\n                return markdownToken.items.map((item) => [\n                    EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_LIST_ITEM_MARKER,\n                    ...joinEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(createEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(item.tokens)),\n                ]);\n            case 'code':\n                return [[<code key=\"code\" className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME}>{markdownToken.text}</code>]];\n            case 'table':\n                return [markdownToken.header, ...markdownToken.rows].map((row) =>\n                    joinEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(\n                        row.map((cell) => renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(cell.tokens, 'inline')),\n                    ),\n                );\n            default:\n                return [\n                    'tokens' in markdownToken && markdownToken.tokens !== undefined\n                        ? renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(markdownToken.tokens, 'inline')\n                        : [readMarkdownTokenText(markdownToken)],\n                ];\n        }\n    });\n}\n\nfunction joinEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(runs: readonly (readonly ReactNode[])[]): readonly ReactNode[] {\n    return runs.flatMap((run, index) => [\n        ...(index === 0 ? [] : [EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_BLOCK_SEPARATOR]),\n        <Fragment key={`run-${index}`}>{run}</Fragment>,\n    ]);\n}\n\ntype EventDescriptionProps = {\n    /**\n     * The words an administrator wrote about one event, written as Markdown\n     */\n    readonly description: string;\n\n    /**\n     * How much room they are read in, see `EVENT_DESCRIPTION_SHAPES`\n     */\n    readonly shape?: EventDescriptionShape;\n    readonly className?: string;\n};\n\n/**\n * The description of one event, read as the Markdown it was written in\n *\n * Note: This is the one place which decides how an authored description reads, so the door of a room, the card a term\n *       is chosen with and the recap of a workshop can never interpret the same words differently. The description\n *       carries no markup of its own: raw HTML only ever contributes its text, an image is read by its label, and only\n *       an address of a known protocol ever becomes a link.\n * Note: The formatting takes no colours of its own and inherits the ones of the surface it is read on, so the fixed\n *       palette of a landing page and the appearance a member chose for their room both stay intact. What does need a\n *       colour — a link, a quotation, a block of code — only ever appears in the whole passage, which is read inside a\n *       room.\n */\nexport function EventDescription({ description, shape = 'block', className }: EventDescriptionProps) {\n    const tokens = readMarkdownTokens(description);\n\n    if (shape === 'inline') {\n        return (\n            <span className={className}>\n                {joinEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(createEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(tokens))}\n            </span>\n        );\n    }\n\n    return <div className={className}>{renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(tokens)}</div>;\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":94,"oldLines":7,"newStart":94,"newLines":7,"lines":["                 ? readMarkdownTokenText(token)","                 : renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape);","         default:","-            // Raw HTML and anything else only ever contributes its text, so a description can carry no markup of its own.","+            // Raw HTML and anything else contributes its text alone, so a description carries no markup of its own.","             return readMarkdownTokenText(token);","     }"," }"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false}}

An `inline` one is the very same words as one flowing excerpt, because the card a term is chosen with\n *       is a single button: block elements and destinations inside a button are neither valid nor clickable, and the\n *       compact card cuts the excerpt off after two lines anyway. Both read the same Markdown, so a term is never\n *       described in two different ways — only at two different lengths.\n */\nexport const EVENT_DESCRIPTION_SHAPES = ['block', 'inline'] as const;\n\nexport type EventDescriptionShape = (typeof EVENT_DESCRIPTION_SHAPES)[number];\n\n/**\n * Protocols a description may lead out to, which leaves `javascript:` and `data:` addresses as plain labels\n */\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_ALLOWED_LINK_PROTOCOLS = new Set(['https:', 'http:', 'mailto:']);\n\n/**\n * What an excerpt puts between two blocks of the description and in front of each item of a list\n */\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_BLOCK_SEPARATOR = ' ';\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_LIST_ITEM_MARKER = '• ';\n\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME = 'font-mono text-[0.95em]';\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME = 'mt-3 first:mt-0';\n\n/**\n * The address of a link which may be opened, or `null` for one which stays a label\n *\n * Note: A site-relative address is kept as it was written, because a description has no page of its own to resolve it\n *       against. A protocol-relative `//host` one is refused, so it can never leave the site unnoticed.\n */\nfunction resolveEventDescriptionHref(href: string): string | null {\n    if (href.startsWith('/')) {\n        return href.startsWith('//') ? null : href;\n    }\n\n    try {\n        const url = new URL(href);\n\n        return EVENT_DESCRIPTION_ALLOWED_LINK_PROTOCOLS.has(url.protocol) ? url.href : null;\n    } catch {\n        // An address which is not an address at all remains readable as a label.\n        return null;\n    }\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionLink(token: Tokens.Link, shape: EventDescriptionShape): ReactNode {\n    const label = renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape);\n    const href = resolveEventDescriptionHref(token.href);\n\n    if (shape === 'inline' || href === null) {\n        return label;\n    }\n\n    // Note: A description is read on the way into a room, so its links open beside it rather than taking a\n    //       participant out of the door they are standing in.\n    return (\n        <a\n            href={href}\n            target=\"_blank\"\n            rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\n            className=\"font-semibold text-room-accent underline decoration-room-accent/50 underline-offset-2 transition hover:text-room-heading\"\n        >\n            {label}\n        </a>\n    );\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionInlineToken(token: MarkedToken, shape: EventDescriptionShape): ReactNode {\n    switch (token.type) {\n        case 'strong':\n            return <strong className=\"font-semibold\">{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</strong>;\n        case 'em':\n            return <em>{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</em>;\n        case 'del':\n            return <del>{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</del>;\n        case 'codespan':\n            return <code className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME}>{token.text}</code>;\n        case 'br':\n            return shape === 'inline' ? EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_BLOCK_SEPARATOR : <br />;\n        case 'link':\n            return renderEventDescriptionLink(token, shape);\n        case 'image':\n            // A description is a passage of text rather than a gallery, so an image is read by what it was called.\n            return readMarkdownTokenText(token) || token.href;\n        case 'text':\n            return token.tokens === undefined\n                ? readMarkdownTokenText(token)\n                : renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape);\n        default:\n            // Raw HTML and anything else contributes its text alone, so a description carries no markup of its own.\n            return readMarkdownTokenText(token);\n    }\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(\n    tokens: readonly Token[],\n    shape: EventDescriptionShape,\n): readonly ReactNode[] {\n    return tokens.map((token, index) => (\n        <Fragment key={`${token.type}-${index}`}>\n            {renderEventDescriptionInlineToken(token as MarkedToken, shape)}\n        </Fragment>\n    ));\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(tokens: readonly Token[]): readonly ReactNode[] {\n    return tokens.flatMap((token, index): readonly ReactNode[] => {\n        const markdownToken = token as MarkedToken;\n        const key = `${markdownToken.type}-${index}`;\n\n        switch (markdownToken.type) {\n            case 'space':\n            case 'def':\n                return [];\n            case 'heading':\n                // Note: A description is one passage rather than a document of its own, so an authored heading leads\n                //       its paragraph instead of claiming a level in the outline of the page around it.\n                return [\n                    <p key={key} className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} font-semibold`}>\n                        {renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(markdownToken.tokens, 'block')}\n                    </p>,\n                ];\n            case 'list': {\n                const items = markdownToken.items.map((item, itemIndex) => (\n                    <li key={`item-${itemIndex}`}>{renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(item.tokens)}</li>\n                ));\n\n                return [\n                    markdownToken.ordered ? (\n                        <ol\n                            key={key}\n                            start={Number(markdownToken.start) || 1}\n                            className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} list-decimal space-y-1 pl-5`}\n                        >\n                            {items}\n                        </ol>\n                    ) : (\n                        <ul key={key} className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} list-disc space-y-1 pl-5`}>\n                            {items}\n                        </ul>\n                    ),\n                ];\n            }\n            case 'blockquote':\n                return [\n                    <blockquote\n                        key={key}\n                        className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} border-l-2 border-room-border/20 pl-3 italic`}\n                    >\n                        {renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(markdownToken.tokens)}\n                    </blockquote>,\n                ];\n            case 'code':\n                return [\n                    <pre\n } from 'vitest';\n\nconst FORMATTED_DESCRIPTION = [\n    '## Co se naučíte',\n    '',\n    'Celé workflow **od issue po merge**, včetně `git rebase` a *code review*.',\n    '',\n    '- rozpad úkolů',\n    '- [materiály](https://ptbk.io/materialy)',\n].join('\\n');\n\ndescribe('event description', () => {\n    afterEach(cleanup);\n\n    it('reads the whole passage an administrator wrote, merge').tagName).toBe('STRONG');\n        expect(screen.getByText('code review').tagName).toBe('EM');\n        expect(screen.getByText('git rebase').tagName).toBe('CODE');\n        expect(container.querySelectorAll('li')).toHaveLength(2);\n\n        const materialsLink = screen.getByRole('link', { name: 'materiály' });\n        expect(materialsLink.getAttribute('href')).toBe('https://ptbk.io/materialy');\n        expect(materialsLink.getAttribute('target')).toBe('_blank');\n        expect(materialsLink.getAttribute('rel')).toBe('noopener noreferrer');\n        expect(container.textContent).not.toContain('**');\n        expect(container.textContent).not.toContain('##');\n    });\n\n    it('keeps an authored heading a lead-in rather than a level of the page it is read on', () => {\n        const { container } = render(<EventDescription description={FORMATTED_DESCRIPTION} />);\n\n        expect(container.querySelector('h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6')).toBeNull();\n        expect(screen.getByText('Co se naučíte').tagName).toBe('P');\n    });\n\n    it('says the same words as one flowing excerpt where a card offers the term', () => {\n        const { container } = render(<EventDescription description={FORMATTED_DESCRIPTION} shape=\"inline\" />);\n\n        expect(screen.getByText('od issue po merge').tagName).toBe('STRONG');\n        expect(screen.getByText('git rebase').tagName).toBe('CODE');\n        expect(container.textContent).toContain('• rozpad úkolů');\n        expect(container.textContent).not.toContain('\\n');\n        expect(container.querySelectorAll('p, ul, ol, li, br')).toHaveLength(0);\n    });\n\n    it('never puts a destination inside the one button a term is chosen with', () => {\n        const { container } = render(<EventDescription description={FORMATTED_DESCRIPTION} shape=\"inline\" />);\n\n        expect(container.querySelector('a')).toBeNull();\n        expect(container.textContent).toContain('materiály');\n        expect(container.textContent).not.toContain('https://ptbk.io/materialy');\n    });\n\n    it('carries no markup of its own and leads only to addresses of a known protocol', () => {\n        const { container } = render(\n            <EventDescription\n                description={\n                    '<script>alert(1)</script> <b>html</b> ![obrázek](https://ptbk.io/i.png)\\n\\n' +\n                    '[skript](javascript:alert(1)) [cizí](//example.com) [komunita](/cs/komunita)'\n                }\n            />,\n        );\n\n        expect(container.querySelector('script')).toBeNull();\n        expect(container.querySelector('b')).toBeNull();\n        expect(container.querySelector('img')).toBeNull();\n        expect(container.textContent).toContain('obrázek');\n        expect(screen.queryByRole('link', { name: 'skript' })).toBeNull();\n        expect(screen.queryByRole('link', { name: 'cizí' })).toBeNull();\n        expect(screen.getByRole('link', { name: 'komunita' }).getAttribute('href')).toBe('/cs/komunita');\n    });\n\n    it('leaves The description carries no markup of its own: raw HTML only\n *       ever contributes its text, an image is read by its label, and only an address of a known protocol ever becomes\n *       a link.","originalFile":"import { readMarkdownTokenText, readMarkdownTokens } from '@/lib/text/markdownText';\nimport type { MarkedToken, Token, Tokens } from 'marked';\nimport { Fragment, type ReactNode } from 'react';\n\n/**\n * How much room an authored description is read in\n *\n * Note: A `block` description is the whole passage an administrator wrote, with its paragraphs, its lists and its\n *       links. An `inline` one is the very same words as one flowing excerpt, because the card a term is chosen with\n *       is a single button: block elements and destinations inside a button are neither valid nor clickable, and the\n *       compact card cuts the excerpt off after two lines anyway. Both read the same Markdown, so a term is never\n *       described in two different ways — only at two different lengths.\n */\nexport const EVENT_DESCRIPTION_SHAPES = ['block', 'inline'] as const;\n\nexport type EventDescriptionShape = (typeof EVENT_DESCRIPTION_SHAPES)[number];\n\n/**\n * Protocols a description may lead out to, which leaves `javascript:` and `data:` addresses as plain labels\n */\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_ALLOWED_LINK_PROTOCOLS = new Set(['https:', 'http:', 'mailto:']);\n\n/**\n * What an excerpt puts between two blocks of the description and in front of each item of a list\n */\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_BLOCK_SEPARATOR = ' ';\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_LIST_ITEM_MARKER = '• ';\n\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME = 'font-mono text-[0.95em]';\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME = 'mt-3 first:mt-0';\n\n/**\n * The address of a link which may be opened, or `null` for one which stays a label\n *\n * Note: A site-relative address is kept as it was written, because a description has no page of its own to resolve it\n *       against. A protocol-relative `//host` one is refused, so it can never leave the site unnoticed.\n */\nfunction resolveEventDescriptionHref(href: string): string | null {\n    if (href.startsWith('/')) {\n        return href.startsWith('//') ? null : href;\n    }\n\n    try {\n        const url = new URL(href);\n\n        return EVENT_DESCRIPTION_ALLOWED_LINK_PROTOCOLS.has(url.protocol) ? url.href : null;\n    } catch {\n        // An address which is not an address at all remains readable as a label.\n        return null;\n    }\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionLink(token: Tokens.Link, shape: EventDescriptionShape): ReactNode {\n    const label = renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape);\n    const href = resolveEventDescriptionHref(token.href);\n\n    if (shape === 'inline' || href === null) {\n        return label;\n    }\n\n    // Note: A description is read on the way into a room, so its links open beside it rather than taking a\n    //       participant out of the door they are standing in.\n    return (\n        <a\n            href={href}\n            target=\"_blank\"\n            rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\n            className=\"font-semibold text-room-accent underline decoration-room-accent/50 underline-offset-2 transition hover:text-room-heading\"\n        >\n            {label}\n        </a>\n    );\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionInlineToken(token: MarkedToken, shape: EventDescriptionShape): ReactNode {\n    switch (token.type) {\n        case 'strong':\n            return <strong className=\"font-semibold\">{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</strong>;\n        case 'em':\n            return <em>{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</em>;\n        case 'del':\n            return <del>{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</del>;\n        case 'codespan':\n            return <code className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME}>{token.text}</code>;\n        case 'br':\n            return shape === 'inline' ? EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_BLOCK_SEPARATOR : <br />;\n        case 'link':\n            return renderEventDescriptionLink(token, shape);\n        case 'image':\n            // A description is a passage of text rather than a gallery, so an image is read by what it was called.\n            return readMarkdownTokenText(token) || token.href;\n        case 'text':\n            return token.tokens === undefined\n                ? readMarkdownTokenText(token)\n                : renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape);\n        default:\n            // Raw HTML and anything else contributes its text alone, so a description carries no markup of its own.\n            return readMarkdownTokenText(token);\n    }\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(\n    tokens: readonly Token[],\n    shape: EventDescriptionShape,\n): readonly ReactNode[] {\n    return tokens.map((token, index) => (\n        <Fragment key={`${token.type}-${index}`}>\n            {renderEventDescriptionInlineToken(token as MarkedToken, shape)}\n        </Fragment>\n    ));\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(tokens: readonly Token[]): readonly ReactNode[] {\n    return tokens.flatMap((token, index): readonly ReactNode[] => {\n        const markdownToken = token as MarkedToken;\n        const key = `${markdownToken.type}-${index}`;\n\n        switch (markdownToken.type) {\n            case 'space':\n            case 'def':\n                return [];\n            case 'heading':\n                // Note: A description is one passage rather than a document of its own, so an authored heading leads\n                //       its paragraph instead of claiming a level in the outline of the page around it.\n                return [\n                    <p key={key} className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} font-semibold`}>\n                        {renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(markdownToken.tokens, 'block')}\n                    </p>,\n                ];\n            case 'list': {\n                const items = markdownToken.items.map((item, itemIndex) => (\n                    <li key={`item-${itemIndex}`}>{renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(item.tokens)}</li>\n                ));\n\n                return [\n                    markdownToken.ordered ? (\n                        <ol\n                            key={key}\n                            start={Number(markdownToken.start) || 1}\n                            className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} list-decimal space-y-1 pl-5`}\n                        >\n                            {items}\n                        </ol>\n                    ) : (\n                        <ul key={key} className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} list-disc space-y-1 pl-5`}>\n                            {items}\n                        </ul>\n                    ),\n                ];\n            }\n            case 'blockquote':\n                return [\n                    <blockquote\n                        key={key}\n                        className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} border-l-2 border-room-border/20 pl-3 italic`}\n                    >\n                        {renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(markdownToken.tokens)}\n                    </blockquote>,\n                ];\n            case 'code':\n                return [\n                    <pre\n                        key={key}\n                        className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} max-w-full overflow-x-auto rounded bg-room-overlay/[0.06] p-2`}\n                    >\n                        <code className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME}>{markdownToken.text}</code>\n                    </pre>,\n                ];\n            case 'hr':\n                return [<hr key={key} className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} border-room-border/20`} />];\n            case 'table':\n                return [\n                    <table\n                        key={key}\n                        className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} block max-w-full overflow-x-auto`}\n                    >\n                        <thead>\n                            <tr>\n                                {markdownToken.header.map((cell, cellIndex) => (\n                                    <th key={`header-${cellIndex}`} className=\"pr-4 text-left font-semibold\">\n                                        {renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(cell.tokens, 'block')}\n                                    </th>\n                                ))}\n                            </tr>\n                        </thead>\n                        <tbody>\n                            {markdownToken.rows.map((row, rowIndex) => (\n                                <tr key={`row-${rowIndex}`}>\n                                    {row.map((cell, cellIndex) => (\n                                        <td key={`cell-${cellIndex}`} className=\"pr-4 align-top\">\n                                            {renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(cell.tokens, 'block')}\n                                        </td>\n                                    ))}\n                                </tr>\n                            ))}\n                        </tbody>\n                    </table>,\n                ];\n            default:\n                return [\n                    <p key={key} className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME}>\n                        {'tokens' in markdownToken && markdownToken.tokens !== undefined\n                            ? renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(markdownToken.tokens, 'block')\n                            : readMarkdownTokenText(markdownToken)}\n                    </p>,\n                ];\n        }\n    });\n}\n\n/**\n * Every block of a description as its own run of inline nodes, in the order it was written\n */\nfunction createEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(tokens: readonly Token[]): readonly (readonly ReactNode[])[] {\n    return tokens.flatMap((token): readonly (readonly ReactNode[])[] => {\n        const markdownToken = token as MarkedToken;\n\n        switch (markdownToken.type) {\n            case 'space':\n            case 'def':\n            case 'hr':\n                return [];\n            case 'blockquote':\n                return createEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(markdownToken.tokens);\n            case 'heading':\n                // An authored heading leads its paragraph in an excerpt exactly as it does in the whole passage.\n                return [\n                    [\n                        <strong key=\"heading\" className=\"font-semibold\">\n                            {renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(markdownToken.tokens, 'inline')}\n                        </strong>,\n                    ],\n                ];\n            case 'list':\n                // An excerpt has no bullets to indent, so each item says that it is one.\n                return markdownToken.items.map((item) => [\n                    EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_LIST_ITEM_MARKER,\n                    ...joinEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(createEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(item.tokens)),\n                ]);\n            case 'code':\n                return [\n                    [\n                        <code key=\"code\" className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME}>\n                            {markdownToken.text}\n                        </code>,\n                    ],\n                ];\n            case 'table':\n                return [markdownToken.header, ...markdownToken.rows].map((row) =>\n                    joinEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(\n                        row.map((cell) => renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(cell.tokens, 'inline')),\n                    ),\n                );\n            default:\n                return [\n                    'tokens' in markdownToken && markdownToken.tokens !== undefined\n                        ? renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(markdownToken.tokens, 'inline')\n                        : [readMarkdownTokenText(markdownToken)],\n                ];\n        }\n    });\n}\n\nfunction joinEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(runs: readonly (readonly ReactNode[])[]): readonly ReactNode[] {\n    return runs.flatMap((run, index) => [\n        ...(index === 0 ? [] : [EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_BLOCK_SEPARATOR]),\n        <Fragment key={`run-${index}`}>{run}</Fragment>,\n    ]);\n}\n\ntype EventDescriptionProps = {\n    /**\n     * The words an administrator wrote about one event, written as Markdown\n     */\n    readonly description: string;\n\n    /**\n     * How much room they are read in, see `EVENT_DESCRIPTION_SHAPES`\n     */\n    readonly shape?: EventDescriptionShape;\n    readonly className?: string;\n};\n\n/**\n * The description of one event, read as the Markdown it was written in\n *\n * Note: This is the one place which decides how an authored description reads, so the door of a room, the card a term\n *       is chosen with and the recap of a workshop can never interpret the same words differently. The description\n *       carries no markup of its own: raw HTML only ever contributes its text, an image is read by its label, and only\n *       an address of a known protocol ever becomes a link.\n * Note: The formatting takes no colours of its own and inherits the ones of the surface it is read on, so the fixed\n *       palette of a landing page and the appearance a member chose for their room both stay intact. What does need a\n *       colour — a link, a quotation, a block of code — only ever appears in the whole passage, which is read inside a\n *       room.\n */\nexport function EventDescription({ description, shape = 'block', className }: EventDescriptionProps) {\n    const tokens = readMarkdownTokens(description);\n\n    if (shape === 'inline') {\n        return (\n            <span className={className}>\n                {joinEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(createEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(tokens))}\n            </span>\n        );\n    }\n\n    return <div className={className}>{renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(tokens)}</div>;\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":284,"oldLines":10,"newStart":284,"newLines":11,"lines":[" /**","  * The description of one event, read as the Markdown it was written in","  *","- * Note: This is the one place which decides how an authored description reads, so the door of a room, the card a term","- *       is chosen with and the recap of a workshop can never interpret the same words differently. [] : [[text]];\n            }\n        }\n    });\n}","originalFile":"import { readMarkdownTokenText, readMarkdownTokens } from '@/lib/text/markdownText';\nimport type { MarkedToken, Token, Tokens } from 'marked';\nimport { Fragment, type ReactNode } from 'react';\n\n/**\n * How much room an authored description is read in\n *\n * Note: A `block` description is the whole passage an administrator wrote, with its paragraphs, its lists and its\n *       links. An `inline` one is the very same words as one flowing excerpt, because the card a term is chosen with\n *       is a single button: block elements and destinations inside a button are neither valid nor clickable, and the\n *       compact card cuts the excerpt off after two lines anyway. Both read the same Markdown, so a term is never\n *       described in two different ways — only at two different lengths.\n */\nexport const EVENT_DESCRIPTION_SHAPES = ['block', 'inline'] as const;\n\nexport type EventDescriptionShape = (typeof EVENT_DESCRIPTION_SHAPES)[number];\n\n/**\n * Protocols a description may lead out to, which leaves `javascript:` and `data:` addresses as plain labels\n */\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_ALLOWED_LINK_PROTOCOLS = new Set(['https:', 'http:', 'mailto:']);\n\n/**\n * What an excerpt puts between two blocks of the description and in front of each item of a list\n */\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_BLOCK_SEPARATOR = ' ';\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_LIST_ITEM_MARKER = '• ';\n\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME = 'font-mono text-[0.95em]';\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME = 'mt-3 first:mt-0';\n\n/**\n * The address of a link which may be opened, or `null` for one which stays a label\n *\n * Note: A site-relative address is kept as it was written, because a description has no page of its own to resolve it\n *       against. A protocol-relative `//host` one is refused, so it can never leave the site unnoticed.\n */\nfunction resolveEventDescriptionHref(href: string): string | null {\n    if (href.startsWith('/')) {\n        return href.startsWith('//') ? null : href;\n    }\n\n    try {\n        const url = new URL(href);\n\n        return EVENT_DESCRIPTION_ALLOWED_LINK_PROTOCOLS.has(url.protocol) ? url.href : null;\n    } catch {\n        // An address which is not an address at all remains readable as a label.\n        return null;\n    }\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionLink(token: Tokens.Link, shape: EventDescriptionShape): ReactNode {\n    const label = renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape);\n    const href = resolveEventDescriptionHref(token.href);\n\n    if (shape === 'inline' || href === null) {\n        return label;\n    }\n\n    // Note: A description is read on the way into a room, so its links open beside it rather than taking a\n    //       participant out of the door they are standing in.\n    return (\n        <a\n            href={href}\n            target=\"_blank\"\n            rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\n            className=\"font-semibold text-room-accent underline decoration-room-accent/50 underline-offset-2 transition hover:text-room-heading\"\n        >\n            {label}\n        </a>\n    );\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionInlineToken(token: MarkedToken, shape: EventDescriptionShape): ReactNode {\n    switch (token.type) {\n        case 'strong':\n            return <strong className=\"font-semibold\">{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</strong>;\n        case 'em':\n            return <em>{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</em>;\n        case 'del':\n            return <del>{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</del>;\n        case 'codespan':\n            return <code className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME}>{token.text}</code>;\n        case 'br':\n            return shape === 'inline' ? EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_BLOCK_SEPARATOR : <br />;\n        case 'link':\n            return renderEventDescriptionLink(token, shape);\n        case 'image':\n            // A description is a passage of text rather than a gallery, so an image is read by what it was called.\n            return readMarkdownTokenText(token) || token.href;\n        case 'text':\n            return token.tokens === undefined\n                ? readMarkdownTokenText(token)\n                : renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape);\n        default:\n            // Raw HTML and anything else contributes its text alone, so a description carries no markup of its own.\n            return readMarkdownTokenText(token);\n    }\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(\n    tokens: readonly Token[],\n    shape: EventDescriptionShape,\n): readonly ReactNode[] {\n    return tokens.map((token, index) => (\n        <Fragment key={`${token.type}-${index}`}>\n            {renderEventDescriptionInlineToken(token as MarkedToken, shape)}\n        </Fragment>\n    ));\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(tokens: readonly Token[]): readonly ReactNode[] {\n    return tokens.flatMap((token, index): readonly ReactNode[] => {\n        const markdownToken = token as MarkedToken;\n        const key = `${markdownToken.type}-${index}`;\n\n        switch (markdownToken.type) {\n            case 'space':\n            case 'def':\n                return [];\n            case 'heading':\n                // Note: A description is one passage rather than a document of its own, so an authored heading leads\n                //       its paragraph instead of claiming a level in the outline of the page around it.\n                return [\n                    <p key={key} className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} font-semibold`}>\n                        {renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(markdownToken.tokens, 'block')}\n                    </p>,\n                ];\n            case 'list': {\n                const items = markdownToken.items.map((item, itemIndex) => (\n                    <li key={`item-${itemIndex}`}>{renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(item.tokens)}</li>\n                ));\n\n                return [\n                    markdownToken.ordered ? (\n                        <ol\n                            key={key}\n                            start={Number(markdownToken.start) || 1}\n                            className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} list-decimal space-y-1 pl-5`}\n                        >\n                            {items}\n                        </ol>\n                    ) : (\n                        <ul key={key} className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} list-disc space-y-1 pl-5`}>\n                            {items}\n                        </ul>\n                    ),\n                ];\n            }\n            case 'blockquote':\n                return [\n                    <blockquote\n                        key={key}\n                        className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} border-l-2 border-room-border/20 pl-3 italic`}\n                    >\n                        {renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(markdownToken.tokens)}\n                    </blockquote>,\n                ];\n            case 'code':\n                return [\n                    <pre\n                        key={key}\n                        className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} max-w-full overflow-x-auto rounded bg-room-overlay/[0.06] p-2`}\n                    >\n                        <code className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME}>{markdownToken.text}</code>\n                    </pre>,\n                ];\n            case 'hr':\n                return [<hr key={key} className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} border-room-border/20`} />];\n            case 'table':\n                return [\n                    <table\n                        key={key}\n                        className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} block max-w-full overflow-x-auto`}\n                    >\n                        <thead>\n                            <tr>\n                                {markdownToken.header.map((cell, cellIndex) => (\n                                    <th key={`header-${cellIndex}`} className=\"pr-4 text-left font-semibold\">\n                                        {renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(cell.tokens, 'block')}\n                                    </th>\n                                ))}\n                            </tr>\n                        </thead>\n                        <tbody>\n                            {markdownToken.rows.map((row, rowIndex) => (\n                                <tr key={`row-${rowIndex}`}>\n                                    {row.map((cell, cellIndex) => (\n                                        <td key={`cell-${cellIndex}`} className=\"pr-4 align-top\">\n                                            {renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(cell.tokens, 'block')}\n                                        </td>\n                                    ))}\n                                </tr>\n                            ))}\n                        </tbody>\n                    </table>,\n                ];\n            default:\n                return [\n                    <p key={key} className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME}>\n                        {'tokens' in markdownToken && markdownToken.tokens !== undefined\n Both read the same Markdown, so a term is never\n *       described in two different ways — only at two different lengths.\n */\nexport const EVENT_DESCRIPTION_SHAPES = ['block', 'inline'] as const;\n\nexport type EventDescriptionShape = (typeof EVENT_DESCRIPTION_SHAPES)[number];\n\n/**\n * Protocols a description may lead out to, which leaves `javascript:` and `data:` addresses as plain labels\n */\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_ALLOWED_LINK_PROTOCOLS = new Set(['https:', 'http:', 'mailto:']);\n\n/**\n * What an excerpt puts between two blocks of the description and in front of each item of a list\n */\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_BLOCK_SEPARATOR = ' ';\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_LIST_ITEM_MARKER = '• ';\n\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME = 'font-mono text-[0.95em]';\nconst EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME = 'mt-3 first:mt-0';\n\n/**\n * The address of a link which may be opened, or `null` for one which stays a label\n *\n * Note: A site-relative address is kept as it was written, because a description has no page of its own to resolve it\n *       against. A protocol-relative `//host` one is refused, so it can never leave the site unnoticed.\n */\nfunction resolveEventDescriptionHref(href: string): string | null {\n    if (href.startsWith('/')) {\n        return href.startsWith('//') ? null : href;\n    }\n\n    try {\n        const url = new URL(href);\n\n        return EVENT_DESCRIPTION_ALLOWED_LINK_PROTOCOLS.has(url.protocol) ? url.href : null;\n    } catch {\n        // An address which is not an address at all remains readable as a label.\n        return null;\n    }\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionLink(token: Tokens.Link, shape: EventDescriptionShape): ReactNode {\n    const label = renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape);\n    const href = resolveEventDescriptionHref(token.href);\n\n    if (shape === 'inline' || href === null) {\n        return label;\n    }\n\n    // Note: A description is read on the way into a room, so its links open beside it rather than taking a\n    //       participant out of the door they are standing in.\n    return (\n        <a\n            href={href}\n            target=\"_blank\"\n            rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\n            className=\"font-semibold text-room-accent underline decoration-room-accent/50 underline-offset-2 transition hover:text-room-heading\"\n        >\n            {label}\n        </a>\n    );\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionInlineToken(token: MarkedToken, shape: EventDescriptionShape): ReactNode {\n    switch (token.type) {\n        case 'strong':\n            return <strong className=\"font-semibold\">{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</strong>;\n        case 'em':\n            return <em>{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</em>;\n        case 'del':\n            return <del>{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</del>;\n        case 'codespan':\n            return <code className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME}>{token.text}</code>;\n        case 'br':\n            return shape === 'inline' ? EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_BLOCK_SEPARATOR : <br />;\n        case 'link':\n            return renderEventDescriptionLink(token, shape);\n        case 'image':\n            // A description is a passage of text rather than a gallery, so an image is read by what it was called.\n            return readMarkdownTokenText(token) || token.href;\n        case 'text':\n            return token.tokens === undefined\n                ? readMarkdownTokenText(token)\n                : renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape);\n        default:\n            // Raw HTML and anything else contributes its text alone, so a description carries no markup of its own.\n            return readMarkdownTokenText(token);\n    }\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(\n    tokens: readonly Token[],\n    shape: EventDescriptionShape,\n): readonly ReactNode[] {\n    return tokens.map((token, index) => (\n        <Fragment key={`${token.type}-${index}`}>\n            {renderEventDescriptionInlineToken(token as MarkedToken, shape)}\n        </Fragment>\n    ));\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(tokens: readonly Token[]): readonly ReactNode[] {\n    return tokens.flatMap((token, index): readonly ReactNode[] => {\n        const markdownToken = token as MarkedToken;\n        const key = `${markdownToken.type}-${index}`;\n\n        switch (markdownToken.type) {\n            case 'space':\n            case 'def':\n                return [];\n            case 'heading':\n                // Note: A description is one passage rather than a document of its own, so an authored heading leads\n                //       its paragraph instead of claiming a level in the outline of the page around it.\n                return [\n                    <p key={key} className={`${EVENT_DESCRIPTION_BLOCK_CLASS_NAME} font-semibold`}>\n                        {renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(markdownToken.tokens, 'block')}\n                    </p>,\n                ];\n            case 'list': {\n                const items = markdownToken.items.map((item, itemIndex) => (\n                    <li key={`item-${itemIndex}`}>{renderEventDescriptionBlockTokens(item.tokens)}</li>\n                ));\n\n                return [\n                    markdownToken.ordered ?  }\n    });\n}\n\n/**\n * Every block of a description as its own run of inline nodes, in the order it was written\n */\nfunction createEventDescriptionExcerptRuns(tokens: readonly Token[]): readonly [] : [EVENT_DESCRIPTION_EXCERPT_BLOCK_SEPARATOR]),\n        <Fragment key={`run-${index}`}>{run}</Fragment>,\n    ]);\n}\n\ntype EventDescriptionProps = {\n    /**\n     * The words an administrator wrote about one event, written as Markdown\n     */\n    readonly description: string;\n\n    /**\n     * How much room they are read in, see `EVENT_DESCRIPTION_SHAPES`\n     */\n    readonly shape?: EventDescriptionShape;\n    readonly className?: string;\n};\n\n/**\n * The description of one event, read as the Markdown it was written in\n *\n * Note: This is the one place which decides how an authored description is read on a page, so the door of a room and\n *       the card a term is chosen with can never interpret the same words differently; the recap PDF reads the very\n *       same Markdown through `createMarkdownPdfContent`. A protocol-relative `//host` one is refused, so it can never leave the site unnoticed.\n */\nfunction resolveEventDescriptionHref(href: string): string | null {\n    if (href.startsWith('/')) {\n        return href.startsWith('//') ? null : href;\n    }\n\n    try {\n        const url = new URL(href);\n\n        return EVENT_DESCRIPTION_ALLOWED_LINK_PROTOCOLS.has(url.protocol) ? url.href : null;\n    } catch {\n        // An address which is not an address at all remains readable as a label.\n        return null;\n    }\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionLink(token: Tokens.Link, shape: EventDescriptionShape): ReactNode {\n    const label = renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape);\n    const href = resolveEventDescriptionHref(token.href);\n\n    if (shape === 'inline' || href === null) {\n        return label;\n    }\n\n    // Note: A description is read on the way into a room, so its links open beside it rather than taking a\n    //       participant out of the door they are standing in.\n    return (\n        <a\n            href={href}\n            target=\"_blank\"\n            rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\n            className=\"font-semibold text-room-accent underline decoration-room-accent/50 underline-offset-2 transition hover:text-room-heading\"\n        >\n            {label}\n        </a>\n    );\n}\n\nfunction renderEventDescriptionInlineToken(token: MarkedToken, shape: EventDescriptionShape): ReactNode {\n    switch (token.type) {\n        case 'strong':\n            return <strong className=\"font-semibold\">{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</strong>;\n        case 'em':\n            return <em>{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</em>;\n        case 'del':\n            return <del>{renderEventDescriptionInlineTokens(token.tokens, shape)}</del>;\n        case 'codespan':\n            return <code className={EVENT_DESCRIPTION_CODE_CLASS_NAME}>{token.text}</code>;\n        case 'br':\n            return shape === 'inline' ?
