{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CfdCsdVf1sazA7B2RLM9K","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Event descriptions now render their Markdown. The whole decision lives in one new place.\n\n## What changed\n\n**`components/events/EventDescription.tsx`** (new) — the one renderer of an authored event description, built on the `marked` lexer the repo already uses for the recap PDF. It has two shapes:\n\n- **`block`** — the whole passage: paragraphs, lists, blockquotes, fenced code, tables, hard breaks, and links that open beside the room. Used by the room door.\n- **`inline`** — the same words as one flowing excerpt, list items prefixed with `•`. Used by the term card, because that card is a single `<button>` where block elements and nested anchors are neither valid HTML nor clickable — and the compact card still clamps to two lines.\n\nBoth are SSR-safe, so the public landing page still ships the description in its HTML. Safety: raw HTML contributes text only, an image reads as its label, and only `https:`/`http:`/`mailto:` or a same-site `/path` becomes a link (`//host` and `javascript:` stay labels). An authored `##` becomes a bold lead-in rather than claiming a heading level in the page around it.\n\n**Surfaces wired up:** the term card (`EventTermOptionCard`) and the room door (`WorkshopConnectionForm`, via `isDescriptionMarkdown` set by the online-workshop and community factories). The wrap-up PDF already read this Markdown. The admin `Popis` field gained a Markdown placeholder and hint.\n\n**`convertMarkdownToPlainText`** in `lib/text/markdownText.ts` flattens it for the participant's calendar entry, which can show no formatting — nothing is dropped, and a link keeps both its label and its destination.\n\n**One deliberate exclusion:** a community project discussion's door keeps plain text. That description is written by a member and passes through the community's moderation, not through a formatter — turning it into live links would cross that boundary. `isDescriptionMarkdown` defaults to off for exactly this reason.\n\n## Verification\n\n`npm run lint`, `tsc`, and the full `vitest` suite pass (the only failure is the known `hostedRecordingMigration` date bomb, which fails at `HEAD` too from 2026-10-01). 21 new unit assertions cover the renderer, the flattener, and both door branches. I ran the e2e specs that actually touch this — `room-theme`, `workshop-wrap-up-pdf`, `admin-autosave`, `public-pages`, `participant-promotion`, `admin-modals`: 45 passed. I did **not** run the full e2e suite; the recording-studio soaks are long and unrelated, and your coder loop runs it next anyway.\n\n## One trade-off worth your call\n\nKeeping one Markdown engine means `marked` is now in the initial bundle of the pages that show descriptions. Measured against `HEAD`: `/cs/online-workshop` 263 kB → 279 kB first-load JS, `/cs/komunita` 321 kB → 336 kB. On the two room routes that is irrelevant, but `/cs/online-workshop` is a public conversion page. The alternative is a second, regex-only formatter for the card (saves ~16 kB there, costs one shared interpretation of the same words). I chose consistency; say the word if you'd rather have the kilobytes."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":955,"cache_read_input_tokens":315559,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":955},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7617c150-9970-4c4e-a550-2e76c168f7b8","uuid":"26255f34-fc41-48ab-a9cf-9fc7b167780e","timestamp":"2026-10-02T09:52:46.954Z","request_id":"req_011CfdCsd1dTVeKZdxuBYjpk"}

The whole decision lives in one new place.\n\n## What changed\n\n**`components/events/EventDescription.tsx`** (new) — the one renderer of an authored event description, built on the `marked` lexer the repo already uses for the recap PDF. It has two shapes:\n\n- **`block`** — the whole passage: paragraphs, lists, blockquotes, fenced code, tables, hard breaks, and links that open beside the room. Used by the room door.\n- **`inline`** — the same words as one flowing excerpt, list items prefixed with `•`. Used by the term card, because that card is a single `<button>` where block elements and nested anchors are neither valid HTML nor clickable — and the compact card still clamps to two lines.\n\nBoth are SSR-safe, so the public landing page still ships the description in its HTML. Safety: raw HTML contributes text only, an image reads as its label, and only `https:`/`http:`/`mailto:` or a same-site `/path` becomes a link (`//host` and `javascript:` stay labels). An authored `##` becomes a bold lead-in rather than claiming a heading level in the page around it.\n\n**Surfaces wired up:** the term card (`EventTermOptionCard`) and the room door (`WorkshopConnectionForm`, via `isDescriptionMarkdown` set by the online-workshop and community factories). The wrap-up PDF already read this Markdown. The admin `Popis` field gained a Markdown placeholder and hint.\n\n**`convertMarkdownToPlainText`** in `lib/text/markdownText.ts` flattens it for the participant's calendar entry, which can show no formatting — nothing is dropped, and a link keeps both its label and its destination.\n\n**One deliberate exclusion:** a community project discussion's door keeps plain text. That description is written by a member and passes through the community's moderation, not through a formatter — turning it into live links would cross that boundary. `isDescriptionMarkdown` defaults to off for exactly this reason.\n\n## Verification\n\n`npm run lint`, `tsc`, and the full `vitest` suite pass (the only failure is the known `hostedRecordingMigration` date bomb, which fails at `HEAD` too from 2026-10-01). 21 new unit assertions cover the renderer, the flattener, and both door branches. I ran the e2e specs that actually touch this — `room-theme`, `workshop-wrap-up-pdf`, `admin-autosave`, `public-pages`, `participant-promotion`, `admin-modals`: 45 passed. I did **not** run the full e2e suite; the recording-studio soaks are long and unrelated, and your coder loop runs it next anyway.\n\n## One trade-off worth your call\n\nKeeping one Markdown engine means `marked` is now in the initial bundle of the pages that show descriptions. Measured against `HEAD`: `/cs/online-workshop` 263 kB → 279 kB first-load JS, `/cs/komunita` 321 kB → 336 kB. On the two room routes that is irrelevant, but `/cs/online-workshop` is a public conversion page. The alternative is a second, regex-only formatter for the card (saves ~16 kB there, costs one shared interpretation of the same words). I chose consistency; say the word if you'd rather have the kilobytes.","ttft_ms":5939,"type":"result","duration_ms":2710017,"uuid":"e1d6e743-674e-410c-95f0-5dc8cf9f6290","ttft_stream_ms":3955,"time_to_request_ms":527,"first_content_frame_ms":3955,"queued_turn_count":0,"result_index":0}
